records.themeTitle: Abraham’s love becomes desire for Torah
records.themeSummary: Longing prepares the way for a genuine new disclosure of Torah.
records.originHebrew: הָאֶחָד כְּנֶגֶד מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, חֶסֶד, דְּרוֹעָא יְמִינָא, וּמִזֶּה בָּא אַהֲבָה: "הוּא הַסֹּבֵב אֵת כָּל אֶרֶץ הַחֲוִילָה", דִּכְתִיב: "הוֹחִילִי לֵאלֹהִים", וְהַיְנוּ כְּשֶׁהוּא לְטוֹבָה; וּכְשֶׁבָּא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְקַלְקְלוֹ וּלְהַפְרִישׁוֹ מֵחָכְמָה "הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיַּחְכִּים יַדְרִים" וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמַּפִּיל עַצְלוּת וְעַצְבוּת עַל הָאָדָם, "עַצְלָה תַּפִּיל תַּרְדֵּמָה"; "אֲשֶׁר שָׁם הַזָּהָב" שֶׁלּוֹקֵחַ הַחֵשֶׁק וְהָאַהֲבָה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא: "מָשְׁכֵהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וְכוּלֵיהּ", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה: "'אֲשֶׁר שָׁם הַזָּהָב' אֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה", וְהוּא טוֹב מְאֹד.
records.originEnglish: The first [river] corresponds to the quality of our father Abraham: kindness, the right arm. From it comes love: “It surrounds the whole land of Havilah,” as in “Hope in God.” This is when it serves the good. When the evil inclination comes to corrupt a person and separate him from wisdom—“One who wishes to become wise should turn south”—it casts indolence and sadness upon him: “Indolence casts one into deep sleep.” “Where there is gold”: one takes that desire and love for words of Torah, in the manner of the Gemara’s instruction, “Draw him to the study hall.” As the Midrash says, “‘Where there is gold’—these are words of Torah.” This is very good.
records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 1
records.targetHebrew: כְּתִיב (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים אָלֶף כָּף חֵית, טֵית) "אִם תִּדְרְשֶׁנּוּ יִמָּצֵא לָךְ", הַדְּרִישָׁה הוּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְהַמְּצִיאָה הוּא יִצְחָק, כִּי עִנְיַן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיָה שֶׁהָיָה מִשְׁתּוֹקֵק תָּמִיד לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה מְאֹד מְאֹד וְשֶׁיִּתְפַּרְסֵם בָּעוֹלָם כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֶלֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶם, וְזֹאת הוּא מִדּוֹת הָאַהֲבָה. וּמִדּוֹת יִצְחָק הוּא מִדּוֹת גְּבוּרָה, הַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר זֹאת וְיָרַד הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְזֹאת יִקָּרֵא גְּבוּרָה כְּמוֹ דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (מְגִילָּה לָמֶד אָלֶף עַמּוּד בֵּית) כָּךְ שָׁמַע מֹשֶׁה מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה. וְיִצְחָק הָיָה גַּם כֵּן נִקְרָא גְּבוּרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם. וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב "וְאֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדוֹת יִצְחָק בֶּן אַבְרָהָם" וְכוּלֵי הַיְינוּ תּוֹלְדוֹת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ הוּא פִּרְסוּם הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, "אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק" הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּקַת אַבְרָהָם הָיְתָה זֹאת, כִּי הַתְּשׁוּקָה הוּא מִדּוֹת אַבְרָהָם, וְכֵן כָּל דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה אֲמִיתִּיִּים אֵין לָהֶם הוֹלָדָה רַק אַחַר גּוֹדֶל תְּשׁוּקָה שֶׁיִּשְׁתּוֹקֵק הָאָדָם לָהֶם.
records.targetEnglish: It is written, “If you seek Him, He will be found by you.” The seeking is our father Abraham, and the finding is Isaac. Abraham’s character was to long intensely, continually, for words of Torah and for it to become known in the world that God reigns over them; this is the quality of love. Isaac’s quality is strength: after this has become clarified and the revelation of God has descended into this world, it is called strength, as the Gemara says, “Thus Moses heard from the mouth of the Almighty.” Isaac too was called God’s strength in the world. “These are the generations of Isaac son of Abraham” thus means that Isaac’s issue is the public revelation of God in this world; “Abraham begot Isaac” means that this came through Abraham’s longing, for longing is Abraham’s quality. Likewise genuine words of Torah can be born only after a person longs intensely for them.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik directs the faculty of love, associated with Abraham, into a desire for Torah that overcomes the inclination’s cooling effect. Mei HaShiloach explains why that redirection is productive: Abraham’s longing is the seeking from which Isaac’s disclosure is born, and genuine Torah likewise comes after great desire. The target develops the generative role of love; Pri Tzadik also gives the separate path of repentance through fear.

records.themeTitle: Repentance can repair a place of real estrangement
records.themeSummary: Great work in returning to God changes how one’s former distance can be understood.
records.originHebrew: וְהַשֵּׁנִי כְּנֶגֶד גְּבוּרָה, מִדַּת פַּחַד יִצְחָק: "הוּא הַסּוֹבֵב אֵת כָּל אֶרֶץ כּוּשׁ", שֶׁמּוֹרֶה שֶׁאַף אִם קִלְקֵל כְּבָר, יוּכַל לְתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ סוֹמֵךְ לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים. וְזֶה עֵסֶק חֹדֶשׁ זֶה: לִהְיוֹת מִבְטַח עֹז בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּשְׁמְרֵהוּ וִיסַיְּעֵהוּ, אַף אִם קִלְקֵל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יוּכַל לְתַקֵּן הַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה.
records.originEnglish: The second [river] corresponds to strength, the quality of Isaac’s fear: “It surrounds the whole land of Cush.” This indicates that even if one has already caused damage, one can repair it through repentance, and God supports all who fall. This is the work of this month: to have strong confidence that God will guard and help one; even if one has caused damage, God forbid, one can repair everything through repentance.
records.targetRef: Tiferet Yosef, Ha'azinu and Shabbat Shuvah 5
records.targetHebrew: והאדם המעמיק בעבודה, אז רואה באמת שבכל המקומות שעמדו בהתרחקות מאד מהשי"ת המה מלאים אור. וזה דאיתא בש"ס (יומא פ"ו:) שב מאהבה זדונות נעשות לו כזכיות, שאחר התשובה ששב אל ד' בגודל עבודה, אז רואה באמת אשר עד הנה היה נדמה לו שעמד בהתרחקות גדול, היה מלא רצונו ית'. וזה ביאור המדרש הנ"ל שהשיב קין לאדם הראשון עשיתי תשובה ונתפשרתי פתח ואמר מזמור שיר ליום השבת, כי אותה הכרה משיג בשלימות ביום השבת, שאז בא שבת בא מנוחה
records.targetEnglish: When a person deepens his service, he truly sees that all the places that stood very far from God are full of light. This is what the Talmud says: one who returns from love has deliberate sins become like merits. After the repentance in which he returns to God with great work, he truly sees that what had until now seemed to stand at a great distance was full of His will. This explains the Midrash: Cain answered Adam, “I repented and reached a settlement,” and Adam began, “A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day.” One attains this recognition fully on Shabbat, when Shabbat comes and rest comes.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik’s confidence includes the possibility of repair after actual damage. Tiferet Yosef explains the depth of that possibility through repentance from love: after great effort in returning, a place that appeared only distant can be recognized as filled with divine light. Both passages locate that disclosure through repentance; the quoted target retains the work that precedes the recognition.

records.themeTitle: The wakeful point beneath spiritual sleep
records.themeSummary: Benjamin represents the divine help that can awaken a person from within.
records.originHebrew: וְהָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה, דְּאִיתָא (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה׳): "'אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה וְלִבִּי עֵר' וְלִבּוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עֵר לְגָאֳלֵנִי וְכוּלֵיהּ; הֵיכָן מָצִינוּ שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל? מִן הַדֵּין קְרָא דִּכְתִיב: 'צוּר לְבָבִי וְחֶלְקִי אֱלֹהִים לְעוֹלָם'", וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁאַף בִּשְׁעַת הַשֵּׁינָה, בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב שׁוֹכֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְעַל כֵּן בִּנְיָמִין שֶׁהַמִּקְדָּשׁ בָּנוּי בְּחֶלְקוֹ, דִּכְתִיב: "וּבֵין כְּתֵפָיו שָׁכֵן", שֶׁהַשְּׁכִינָה שְׁרוּיָה בְּחֶלְקוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זְבָחִים נ״ד עַמּוּד ב׳), עַל כֵּן חִשְּׁבוּ כֹּחַ הַשֵּׁינָה לְבִנְיָמִין.
records.originEnglish: The meaning is explained in Song of Songs Rabbah: “‘I sleep, but my heart is awake’—the heart of the Holy One is awake to redeem me.” Where do we find that the Holy One is Israel’s heart? In the verse, “God is the Rock of my heart and my portion forever.” Even in sleep, God dwells in the depths of the heart. Benjamin’s portion contains the Temple, of which it is written, “He dwells between his shoulders”: the Divine Presence rests in his portion. They therefore assigned the power of sleep to Benjamin.
records.targetHebrew: וְהַסַּיַּיעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא דְּ״אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ — אֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ״ (קִדּוּשִׁין ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּבִנְיָמִין הַנִּטְפָּל תָּמִיד לִיהוּדָה כִּי אֵין כֹּחוֹ כָּל כָּךְ בְּהַגְדָּרַת עַצְמוֹ כְּיוֹסֵף רַק בְּצֵירוּף הַסַּיַּיעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא דְּהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהִיא לְעוֹלָם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (ה:ב): דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״צוּר לְבָבִי וְחֶלְקִי [אֱלֹהִים לְעוֹלָם]״ (תְּהִלִּים ע״ג:כ״ו) וְדָרְשׁוּ עַל זֶה: ״אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה וְלִבִּי עֵר״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ה:ב) הַיְינוּ דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מְשׁוּקָּע בְּדִמְיוֹן שֶׁהוּא הַשֵּׁינָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין הַדִּמְיוֹן נוֹגֵעַ עַד מַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב, דְּשָׁם יֵשׁ לְעוֹלָם נְקֻדַּת ״צוּר לְבָבוֹ״ שֶׁהִיא עֵרָה וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לְהִתְעוֹרֵר מִתַּרְדֵּמָתוֹ,
records.targetEnglish: The heavenly help of “Were the Holy One not to help him, he could not overcome it” is Benjamin’s degree. He is always joined to Judah, for his power of self-restraint is not like Joseph’s; it operates together with heavenly assistance, the resting of God’s Presence wherever it may be. God always dwells in the depths of his heart. As Song of Songs Rabbah says, the Holy One is Israel’s heart: “God is the Rock of my heart and my portion forever.” They expound “I sleep, but my heart is awake” accordingly: even though one is immersed in imagination, which is sleep, imagination does not reach the heart’s depths. There is always the point of the “Rock of his heart,” which remains awake, and through it one can awaken from slumber.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik connects Benjamin’s Temple portion with God dwelling in Israel’s heart even during sleep. Machshavot Charutz explains Benjamin’s particular role beside Joseph: Joseph represents exertion in self-restraint, while Benjamin represents the help that remains rooted deeper than the imagination’s slumber. The inner wakefulness is thus a source from which actual awakening can begin.

records.themeTitle: The Temple joins an enduring gift to human service
records.themeSummary: The holiness already planted within Israel becomes consciously acquired through service.
records.originHebrew: וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁאַף בִּשְׁעַת הַשֵּׁינָה, בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב שׁוֹכֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְעַל כֵּן בִּנְיָמִין שֶׁהַמִּקְדָּשׁ בָּנוּי בְּחֶלְקוֹ, דִּכְתִיב: "וּבֵין כְּתֵפָיו שָׁכֵן", שֶׁהַשְּׁכִינָה שְׁרוּיָה בְּחֶלְקוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זְבָחִים נ״ד עַמּוּד ב׳), עַל כֵּן חִשְּׁבוּ כֹּחַ הַשֵּׁינָה לְבִנְיָמִין.
records.originEnglish: Even in sleep, God dwells in the depths of the heart. Benjamin’s portion contains the Temple, of which it is written, “He dwells between his shoulders”: the Divine Presence rests in his portion, as stated in Zevachim. They therefore assigned the power of sleep to Benjamin.
records.targetHebrew: והנה במקום המקדש היה ניכר מפורש זאת הקדושה דקבוע וקיימא גבי ישראל, ולזה היה נמי שם כל העבודות, כי שם היה ניכר ג"כ מפורש איך שחפץ השי"ת בעבודת ישראל שיבררו עצמם, מדוע באמת בחר השי"ת בישראל יותר מכל האומות, וכדאיתא במדרש (רבה במדבר יג) בעוד שהקב"ה היה יחיד בעולמו היה חפץ להיות לו דירה בתחתונים, היינו שיהיה גבי ישראל כדכתיב (שמות ל״א:י״ג) לדעת כי אני ד' מקדישכם. וזה דאיתא (שם) סבור למבנייה בעין עיטם דמדלי אמרו ניתתי ביה קליל כדכתיב (דברים ל״ג:י״ב) ובין כתפיו שכן. היינו שיברר האדם נגד זאת הקדושה, מדוע נתן לו השי"ת הקדושה הזאת נגד המקטרגים. נמצא שבמקום המקדש היו מתאחדים אלו שני הקדושות, הקדושה שהוא בקביעות מצידו ית' עם הקדושה שהוא על ידי עבודת ישראל, עד שהיה חיבור גמור מתפיסת ישראל עם אורו ית'.
records.targetEnglish: At the place of the Temple this holiness, permanently established in Israel, was manifest. All the services were therefore also there, for it was manifest there how God desires Israel’s service: they should clarify why God chose Israel from among the nations. The Midrash says that while the Holy One was still alone in His world He desired a dwelling below—that Israel should attain “to know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you.” This explains the statement that they considered building it at Ein Eitam, which was higher, but said, “Let us lower it a little,” as it is written, “He dwells between his shoulders”: a person should clarify, in answer to the accusers, why God gave him this holiness. At the Temple these two forms of holiness were therefore united: the holiness permanently established from His side and the holiness through Israel’s service, until there was a complete connection between Israel’s apprehension and His light.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik places Benjamin’s “between his shoulders” beside the divine presence that persists beneath sleep. Tiferet Yosef explains the same Temple location as the meeting of two forms of holiness: God’s established gift and the holiness clarified through Israel’s work. This explains how an enduring inner presence can support an ascent that still calls for human participation.

The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: A descent can make a new relation possible
records.themeSummary: Creation’s sleep opens the way from an original completeness to a face-to-face relation.
records.originHebrew: וְאָז נִזְכַּר אוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ, שֶׁנִּבְרֵאת בְּאוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ, שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי תַּרְדֵּמָה, וְהוּא תְּחִלַּת מַפָּלָה; רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ סוֹמֵךְ לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה נְפִילָה כְּלָל, רַק יְרִידָה שֶׁהִיא צֹרֶךְ עֲלִיָּה.
records.originEnglish: Then the letter samekh appears: [the woman] was created through samekh, through deep sleep, which is the beginning of a fall. But God supports all who fall, so that it should not be a fall at all, only a descent needed for an ascent.
records.targetHebrew: וּתְחִלַּת נְפִילָה — שֵׁינָה, דְּ״וַיַּפֵּל [ה׳ אֱלֹהִים] תַּרְדֵּמָה״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב:כא), כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה י״ז:ה׳) שָׁם עַל פָּסוּק זֶה שֶׁהוּא ״אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בְּמִיתָה״ (בְּרָכוֹת נ״ז עַמּוּד ב׳), שֶׁמִּסְתַּלֵּק הַחָכְמָה וּבִינָה וְכֵן כָּל הַמִּדּוֹת שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ בְּהַתְחָלַת הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁ״הָאֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כט) וּמוּכָן לָשֶׁבֶת בְּגַן עֵדֶן רַק שֶׁרָאָה: ״לֹא טוֹב הֱיוֹת הָאָדָם לְבַדּוֹ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב:יח), בְּסוֹד ״אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ג:י) שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַהַשְׁפָּעָה וּלְהוֹלִיד בְּדוֹמֶה וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּלֹא עֵזֶר ״פָּנִים בְּפָנִים״,
records.targetEnglish: The beginning of a fall is sleep: “God cast a deep sleep,” as Genesis Rabbah says on this verse. Sleep is one sixtieth of death: wisdom and understanding withdraw, as do all the qualities a person had at the beginning of creation, when “God made the human being upright,” prepared to dwell in Eden. But He saw that “it is not good for the human being to be alone,” in the mystery of “Say of the righteous one that he is good”: the power to give and bring forth one like oneself. This is impossible without a helper face to face.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik describes the sleep involved in the woman’s creation as a descent supported toward an ascent. Machshavot Charutz explains what the original condition lacked: the capacity to give and bring forth through a face-to-face helper. Its full paragraph also treats the dangers introduced with separation and their repair. The comparison explains the purpose of this creation-stage descent without turning its dangers into a goal.
records.translationProvenance: New English translations of the unchanged canonical Hebrew excerpts, prepared for this editorial connection. The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: Concealment makes room for work of one’s own
records.themeSummary: The sleep of creation allows a person to seek and understand by choice.
records.originHebrew: וְאָז נִזְכַּר אוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ, שֶׁנִּבְרֵאת בְּאוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ, שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי תַּרְדֵּמָה, וְהוּא תְּחִלַּת מַפָּלָה; רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ סוֹמֵךְ לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה נְפִילָה כְּלָל, רַק יְרִידָה שֶׁהִיא צֹרֶךְ עֲלִיָּה.
records.originEnglish: Then the letter samekh appears: [the woman] was created through samekh, through deep sleep, which is the beginning of a fall. But God supports all who fall, so that it should not be a fall at all, only a descent needed for an ascent.
records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Genesis, Bereshit 7
records.targetHebrew: וַיַּפֵּל ה' אֱלֹהִים תַּרְדֵּמָה עַל הָאָדָם וַיִּישָׁן. זֶה נִכְתַּב אַחַר שֶׁכְּתִיב "וַיִּיצֶר ה' אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם עָפָר מִן הָאֲדָמָה וַיִּפַּח בְּאַפָּיו נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים", וְאִיתָא (בְּסֵפֶר הַקָּנֶה לְמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית) מַאן דְּנָפַח מֵעַצְמוֹ נוֹפֵחַ, וְכֹחַ הַפּוֹעֵל בַּנִּפְעָל, וְלֹא הָיָה נִכָּר בָּאָדָם כֹּחַ יְגִיעַ כַּפָּיו; לָכֵן בְּחֶסֶד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְמַעַן שֶׁלֹּא יֹאכַל הָאָדָם נַהֲמָא דְּכִסּוּפָא הִפִּיל עָלָיו תַּרְדֵּמָה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהִסְתִּיר אֶת אוֹר הַבָּהִיר, וְרַק שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּעַצְמוֹ בִּבְחִירָתוֹ, וּבְעַצְמוֹ יָבִין דַּרְכּוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (וָאֶתְחַנַּן; דְּבָרִים ד, לט) "וְיָדַעְתָּ הַיּוֹם וַהֲשֵׁבֹתָ אֶל לְבָבֶךָ כִּי ה' הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים", וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיֹּאכַל הָאָדָם יְגִיעַ כַּפּוֹ וְאָז אַשְׁרָיו וְטוֹב לוֹ.
records.targetEnglish: “The Lord God cast a deep sleep upon the human being, and he slept.” This is written after “The Lord God formed the human being from the dust of the earth and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.” The Sefer HaKanah says that one who blows, blows from oneself; the actor’s power is in the action’s product. The work of the human being’s own hands was therefore not discernible. In His kindness, so that a person should not eat the bread of shame, God cast a deep sleep upon him: He concealed the clear light, so that the person should exert himself by his own choice and understand his way himself. As it is written, “Know today and bring it back to your heart that the Lord is God.” One then eats the work of one’s own hands and is fortunate and fares well.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik insists that the first sleep can be a supported descent needed for ascent. Mei HaShiloach explains an aspect of that need: the original divine illumination did not yet make human effort discernible as one’s own. Its concealment creates room for chosen effort and understanding. This gives a precise account of how the descent can serve a further good.

The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: Love calls forth answering love
records.themeSummary: The voice of prayer brings the relationship into felt expression.
records.originHebrew: דְּאַבְרָהָם נִקְרָא "אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי", וּבְסִפְרֵי (סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת דְּבָרִים) אִיתָא עַל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "מַה דִּבְלִבָּךְ עַל רְחִימָךְ, מַה דִּבְלִבֵּיהּ עֲלָךְ", וְהוּא כְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כַּמַּיִם הַפָּנִים לַפָּנִים, כֵּן לֵב הָאָדָם לָאָדָם"; וְכֵיוָן דִּכְתִיב "אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי", בְּוַדַּאי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹהֲבוֹ גַּם כֵּן, וְעַל כֵּן נִדְרַשׁ "מֶה לִידִידִי" עַל אַבְרָהָם.
records.originEnglish: Abraham is called “Abraham who loves Me.” The Sifrei says concerning the Holy One, “What is in your heart toward your beloved is what is in his heart toward you.” This is “As water reflects face to face, so the human heart to another.” Since it is written, “Abraham who loves Me,” God certainly loves him too; “What has My beloved [to do in My house]?” is therefore expounded concerning Abraham.
records.targetHebrew: וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְעוֹרֵר יוֹתֵר לִצְעוֹק לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהוֹשִׁיעוֹ וְאֵין סוֹמֵךְ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְעוֹרְרוֹ בְּעַצְמוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְעוֹרֵר אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בִּפְסָחִים קיח:] ״אֵימָתַי אֲנִי אֲהוּבָה — כְּשֶׁיִּשְׁמַע קוֹל תַּחֲנוּנַי״ כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִשְׁתּוֹקֵק לִשְׁמוֹעַ הַקּוֹל ״קוֹל יַעֲקֹב״, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הַשְׁמִיעִנִי אֶת קוֹלֵךְ כִּי קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב״
records.targetEnglish: Through this [his own mistaken sense of being rejected by God] he is stirred more deeply to cry to God to save him, and does not rely on God to awaken him on His own. Through this he awakens God’s love, as our sages say: “When am I beloved? When He hears the voice of my supplication.” For God longs to hear the voice, “the voice of Jacob,” as it is said, “Let Me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet.”
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik explains why Abraham, who loves God, is also called God’s beloved: love answers love. Takanat HaShavin describes this reciprocity in prayer. The person’s own mistaken sense of rejection stirs a deeper cry that awakens the disclosure of divine love. God’s prior awakening already expressed love or mercy, not actual rejection. This supplies an active expression of the relationship stated here.

The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: More divine presence awakens more longing
records.themeSummary: Benjamin’s desire for the Temple illustrates a relationship that deepens through receiving.
records.originHebrew: דְּבִנְיָמִין נִקְרָא "יְדִיד הַשֵּׁם" בְּיִחוּד, שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁשָּׁם הַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּנוּי בְּחֶלְקוֹ;
records.originEnglish: Benjamin is specifically called “the Lord’s beloved,” for the Temple, the place where His Presence rests, is built in his portion.
records.targetHebrew: וכענין מאמרם ז"ל בגמ' (מגילה כו) ורצועה היתה יוצאה מחלקו של יהודה ונכנסת בחלקו של בנימין ובה מזבח בנוי והיה בנימין הצדיק מצטער עליו בכל יום לבולעה שנאמר חופף עליו כל היום לפיכך זכה בנימין הצדיק ונעשה אושפיזכן לשכינה וכו' היינו משום שיודע השי"ת שכל מה שישכון אצל בנימין יותר אור יתוסף אצלו התשוקה ג"כ ביותר לפיכך בחר בו השי"ת לשכון אצלו ונעשה אושפיזכן לשכינה ככה מתעורר ע"י גודל תשוקתם של ישראל שיהיה תמיד אצלם ה' מסיני בא בלי הפסק כלל:
records.targetEnglish: As our sages say: a strip extended from Judah’s portion into Benjamin’s, and the altar was built upon it. The righteous Benjamin was distressed over it every day, longing to absorb it, as it is written, “He shelters him all the day.” Therefore Benjamin merited becoming the host of the Divine Presence. This means that God knows that the more light rests with Benjamin, the more his longing will increase. God therefore chose to dwell with him, and he became the host of the Divine Presence. Likewise Israel’s great longing awakens “the Lord comes from Sinai” among them continually, without interruption.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik singles out Benjamin as God’s beloved and the host of the Temple. Sod Yesharim explains why he becomes the host: God knows that greater illumination will increase Benjamin’s longing still further. This develops the reciprocity of love described in the same originating paragraph through Benjamin’s particular Temple relation.

The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: The inner willing point can become clearer across generations
records.themeSummary: The deeds of those who overcome an inclination deepen the whole community’s hidden capacity.
records.originHebrew: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרְאוּ "יְדִידִים" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא, דְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל רְאוּיִם לְהַשְׁרָאַת הַשְּׁכִינָה, כְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי אֲנִי הַשֵּׁם שֹׁכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל"; אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם טְמֵאִים, שְׁכִינָה שְׁרוּיָה בֵּינֵיהֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסִפְרֵי (סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת מַסְעֵי); וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁבְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב קָשׁוּר הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ, שֶׁ"רְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב וְכוּלֵיהּ" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳).
records.originEnglish: All Israel are called beloved; all Israel are fit for the resting of the Divine Presence. “For I am the Lord who dwells among the children of Israel”: even though they are impure, the Divine Presence rests among them, as the Sifrei says. In the depths of the heart a Jew is bound to the root: “Our will is to do Your will; what prevents us…?”
records.targetHebrew: וּבְכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר יֵשׁ כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה נְפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הַגּוֹדְרִים עַצְמָם בְּאֵיזֶה עִנְיָנִים שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ בָּהֶם לְנִסָּיוֹן, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְנַסֶּה לְעוֹלָם בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר הַקַּנְקַנִּים הַשְּׁלֵמִים צַדִּיקֵי הַדּוֹרוֹת דְּ"לָא בָּצִיר עָלְמָא מִנַּיְיהוּ" (סֻכָּה מ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳), וּבְאוֹתָן הָעִנְיָנִים שֶׁהִשְׁלִימוּ עַצְמָן הֲרֵי נִשְׁלְמוּ כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת הַדּוֹרוֹת כֻּלָּם עִמָּהֶם. וְזֶה טַעַם שֶׁקִּבַּלְתִּי, דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַדּוֹרוֹת הוֹלְכִים וּמִתְקַטְּנִים וְ"לָא אִיכְשׁוּר דָּרֵי", מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַנְּקֻדָּה שֶׁבְּלֵב אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי הוֹלֶכֶת וּמִשְׁתַּלֶּמֶת יוֹתֵר וּמְאִירָה יוֹתֵר בְּכָל דּוֹר עַד עֵת קֵץ שֶׁתִּשְׁתַּלֵּם לְגַמְרֵי; וְהַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁבְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב שֶׁאֵין מִתְגַּלֶּה בְּפֹעַל אֵצֶל כָּל אֶחָד מִצַּד כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הַמַּקִּיף לְכָל אֶחָד, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳): "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ וְכוּ׳ וּמִי מְעַכֵּב וְכוּ׳", וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר הָרַמְבַּ"ם בְּהִלְכוֹת גֵּרוּשִׁין (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב׳) בְּטַעַם "כּוֹפִין עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר רוֹצֶה אֲנִי", דַּאֲמִתַּת רְצוֹנוֹ כָּךְ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין רוֹצֶה בְּפֹעַל עַל פִּי יִצְרוֹ דַּאֲנָסֵיהּ.
records.targetEnglish: In every generation there are many souls of Israel who restrain themselves in matters in which they have entered a trial. God always tests the sound vessels, the righteous of the generations, of whom the world is never lacking; in the matters in which they perfect themselves, all the souls of all generations are perfected with them. This explains a teaching I received: although the generations grow smaller and “the generations have not improved,” the point in the Jewish heart becomes increasingly perfected and shines more in each generation, until the end-time when it will become complete. This concerns the heart’s depths, which do not appear in everyone’s actual conduct because of the inclination surrounding each person. Thus, “It is revealed and known that our will is…” and “what prevents us…”; likewise Rambam explains “we compel him until he says, ‘I am willing’”: his true will is so, although in practice he does not will it because his inclination coerces him.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik invokes the genuine inner will beneath the inclination’s outward resistance. Divrei Soferim explains how that point is strengthened: because Israel forms one whole, the restraint achieved by particular souls becomes rooted in others as well. Its use of the same Rambam gives an account of how the inner willingness can continue to be refined even when outward conduct remains obstructed.

records.themeTitle: Removing resistance reveals an inherited willingness
records.themeSummary: Abraham’s enduring generosity remains rooted beneath a later appearance of refusal.
records.originHebrew: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב׳ מֵהִלְכוֹת גֵּרוּשִׁין): "מֵאַחַר שֶׁהוּא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת כָּל הַמִּצְווֹת וְכוּלֵיהּ, וְיִצְרוֹ תְּקָפוֹ, וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהֻכָּה עַד שֶׁתָּשַׁשׁ יִצְרוֹ כְּבָר גֵּרֵשׁ לִרְצוֹנוֹ וְכוּלֵיהּ"; וְעַל זֶה סוֹמְכִין אַף בְּרָשָׁע שֶׁאָנוּ רוֹאִים שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה, וְאִם יֶחְדְּלוּ מִלְּהַכּוֹתוֹ יְסָרֵב; מִכָּל מָקוֹם סוֹמְכִין אָנוּ שֶׁבְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לְבָבוֹ הוּא רוֹצֶה לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
records.originEnglish: Rambam writes at the end of chapter 2 of the Laws of Divorce: since he is a Jew and wishes to do all the commandments, but his inclination overpowered him, once he is struck until his inclination weakens, he has already divorced willingly. We rely on this even with an evildoer whom we see refusing, who would resist if the beating ceased. Nevertheless, we rely on the fact that in the depths of his heart he wishes to heed the sages and do God’s will.
records.targetHebrew: אבל אאע"ה שהיה דבוק תמיד ברצונו ית' בקביעות גמור לא נשתנה מלבו מעולם עוצם הנדיבות שלו בשום פעם אף בכל התחלפות הזמנים שעבר עליו ולכן אין נמי מקום לקטרג עליו שעבר על לאו דלא יחל פנו ולא ימיר כיון שלא נגרע ממנו עוצם נדבת לבבו בשום פעם אותו נדיבות העצום שהיה בו בהתחלה בפעם הראשון היה אצלו גם בזמן בתרא וכן נשאר לזרעו אחריו זאת הנדיבות בקביעות לזה מצינו בגמרא גבי קרבן שכופין אותו עד שאומר רוצה אני והוא כי באמת נמצא בעומק לבם של ישראל נדיבות עצום אלא מחמת ההסתר שמסתיר בעדו ומונע אותו נראה בו גוון שאינו חפץ להקריב לזה מיד כשכופין זאת המניעה לבלתי יסתיר בעדו ומסירין הימנו זה הגוון אזי נשאר עומד בזה הרצון והנדיבות הנקבע בעומק לבבו מירושת אבות:
records.targetEnglish: Our father Abraham, however, was always firmly attached to His will; the intensity of his generosity never changed in any of the changing times he experienced. There is therefore no ground to accuse him regarding “he shall not exchange or substitute,” since the intensity of his generous heart never diminished. The great generosity present at the first moment remained at the later moment, and this generosity also remained permanently in his descendants. We therefore find in the Gemara concerning an offering that they compel him until he says, “I am willing.” In truth, immense generosity is found in the depths of Israel’s heart. Because concealment hides it and obstructs him, he appears unwilling to offer. As soon as that obstruction is constrained so that it no longer conceals, and that appearance is removed, he remains standing in the willingness and generosity fixed in the depths of his heart as an inheritance from the patriarchs.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik cites the legal case in which outward resistance conceals an inward desire to obey. Sod Yesharim uses the sacrificial case to identify a source for this inward willingness: Abraham’s generosity remained constant through changing circumstances and was transmitted to his descendants. The relation explains the depth being uncovered; the two passages discuss their particular legal examples.

records.themeTitle: The appearance of sleep does not reach the heart
records.themeSummary: Purim reveals an attachment hidden from outward sight.
records.originHebrew: וְאִיתָא (סוֹטָה מ״ח עַמּוּד א׳): "'עוּרָה לָמָּה תִישַׁן' וְכִי יֵשׁ שֵׁינָה לִפְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם וְכוּלֵיהּ? אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל שְׁרוּיִין בְּצַעַר וְכוּלֵיהּ, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: 'עוּרָה לָמָּה תִישַׁן הַשֵּׁם'", וְהַיְנוּ נִרְאֶה כִּבְיָכוֹל אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּשֵׁינָה. וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי אִיתָא (מְגִלָּה ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): "'בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא נָדְדָה שְׁנַת הַמֶּלֶךְ' נָדְדָה שְׁנַת מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם", שֶׁאָז הָיָה נִרְאֶה כְּשֵׁינָה לְמַעְלָה כִּבְיָכוֹל, שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהֶסְתֵּר פָּנִים;
records.originEnglish: The Gemara asks concerning “Awake! Why do You sleep?”: is there sleep before the Omnipresent? Rather, when Israel is in distress, this is why it says, “Awake! Why do You sleep, Lord?” It appears, as it were, like sleep with God. Thus, “‘On that night the king’s sleep was disturbed’—the sleep of the King of the world was disturbed”: Israel was then under concealment of the divine face, which appeared, as it were, like sleep above.
records.targetHebrew: וְטַעֲנַת הָמָן נֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל: שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן ״יְשֵׁנִים מִן הַמִּצְוֹת״ וְאֵינָם מַכִּירִים אֱלָהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר: דְּגַם אֱלֹהֵיהֶם יָשֵׁן הוּא (מְגִלָּה י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳) כִּי אֵין הַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ וּשְׁכִינָתוֹ עוֹד בֵּינֵיהֶם, וְרָצָה ״לְאַבֵּד״ לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה מְצִיאוּת עוֹד לְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת מֵהַשֵּׁינָה אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת נֶאֱמַר בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל: ״אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה — וְלִבִּי עֵר״ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ה:ב) וּבְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ה:ב): דְּהוּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּ״[הִנֵּה] לֹא יָנוּם וְלֹא יִישָׁן שׁוֹמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל״ (תְּהִלִּים קכ״א:ד׳) וּמַה שֶּׁהָיָה כְּעֵין שֵׁינָה בְּגָלוּת בָּבֶל הָיָה רַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן וְלִפְנִים, לָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר ״יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם״ (שְׁמוּאֵל א ט״ז:ז׳) שֶׁבָּהֶם הֶיכֵּר הַשֵּׁינָה וְלֹא לַה׳ אֲשֶׁר ״יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב״ (שָׁם), וְ״לִבִּי עֵר״ וַאֲפִילּוּ כְּשֶׁלְּמַרְאִית הָעַיִן אֵין נִיכָּר שׁוּם קְרִיאַת שֵׁם ה׳ עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם שָׁם הוּא תֹּקֶף הַגִּלּוּי דִּכְבוֹד שָׁמַיִם עַל יָדָם וּבָזֶה נִתְקַן הַכֹּל, דְּכָל מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הָמָן ״נַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא״ (אֶסְתֵּר ט:א) עַל הָאֱמֶת, וּכְמָה שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר:
records.targetEnglish: Haman’s claim against Israel was that they too were “asleep regarding the commandments” and did not recognize His divinity. He therefore said that their God too was asleep: His providence and Presence were no longer among them. He wanted to destroy them altogether, leaving no possibility of awakening from sleep. But concerning the community of Israel it is truly said, “I sleep, but my heart is awake.” Song of Songs Rabbah explains that the Holy One is Israel’s heart, for “the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.” What resembled sleep in the Babylonian exile was only an outward appearance, to the person who “sees with the eyes,” where sleep is recognized—not to God, who “sees the heart,” and “my heart is awake.” Even where outwardly no calling of God’s name upon Israel is recognizable, there too is the powerful disclosure of Heaven’s glory through them. Through this everything is repaired: all of Haman’s thought is truly reversed.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik explains the language of God’s sleep as the appearance produced by Israel’s distress and concealment. Machshavot Charutz develops the contrast between what human eyes see and the heart God sees: Haman mistakes an outward condition for the loss of any possibility of awakening. This explains why the concealment can end in the disclosure of the same enduring relationship.

records.themeTitle: God remains present within the distress
records.themeSummary: The burning bush shows divine patience and companionship during oppression.
records.originHebrew: וְאִיתָא (סוֹטָה מ״ח עַמּוּד א׳): "'עוּרָה לָמָּה תִישַׁן' וְכִי יֵשׁ שֵׁינָה לִפְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם וְכוּלֵיהּ? אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל שְׁרוּיִין בְּצַעַר וְכוּלֵיהּ, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: 'עוּרָה לָמָּה תִישַׁן הַשֵּׁם'", וְהַיְנוּ נִרְאֶה כִּבְיָכוֹל אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּשֵׁינָה.
records.originEnglish: The Gemara asks concerning “Awake! Why do You sleep?”: is there sleep before the Omnipresent? Rather, when Israel is in distress, this is why it says, “Awake! Why do You sleep, Lord?” It appears, as it were, like sleep with God.
records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Shemot 4
records.targetHebrew: וְהִנֵּה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אַחֲרֵי שֶׁבָּרַח מִפְּנֵי פַּרְעֹה לָמַד דַּעַת לִהְיוֹת סַבְלָן, וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן שֶׁנִּרְאָה אֵלָיו הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בַּסְּנֶה לְלַמְּדוֹ זֹאת הַמִּדָּה וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹכֵן בַּסְּנֶה הַיְנוּ סַבְלָן גָּדוֹל כִּי "עִמּוֹ אָנֹכִי בְצָרָה" וְהוּא סַבְלָן נֶגֶד פַּרְעֹה. וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן שֶׁבֵּרַךְ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אֶת יוֹסֵף (דְּבָרִים לָמֶד גִּימֶל, טֵית זַיִן) "וּרְצוֹן שֹׁכְנִי סְנֶה", כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה רוֹצֶה לְהַכְנִיס מִדּוֹת סַבְלָנוּת לְתוֹךְ מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מָלֵא רָצוֹן עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ שׁוּם תַּרְעוֹמוֹת עַל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי מִשֵּׁבֶט הַזֶּה מִתְעוֹרֵר דִּין עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעֵת שֶׁנּוֹטִים מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ שֶׁהַנָּבִיא הִזְהִיר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אָמַר לָהֶם (עָמוֹס הֵא, וָאו) "פֶּן יִצְלַח כָּאֵשׁ בֵּית יוֹסֵף" וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ לֹא תִכְעֹס וְיִהְיֶה בְּרָצוֹן עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, עַל כֵּן אָמַר "וּרְצוֹן שֹׁכְנִי סְנֶה", הַיְנוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְלַמֵּד אוֹתְךָ מִדּוֹת סַבְלָנוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁלִּמֵּד אוֹתִי בַּסְּנֶה.
records.targetEnglish: After fleeing Pharaoh, Moses our teacher learned to be patient. This is why the Holy One appeared to him in the bush: to teach him this quality. He showed him that He dwells in the bush—that He is greatly patient, for “I am with him in distress”—and is patient toward Pharaoh. This is the meaning of Moses’ blessing to Joseph, “the favor of the One who dwells in the bush.” Moses wished to place patience within Joseph the righteous one’s quality, so that he would be full of goodwill toward Israel and have no complaint against any Jewish soul. For judgment against Israel awakens from this tribe when they turn from God’s will, as the prophet warned, “Lest He break out like fire in the house of Joseph.” His quality should not become angry, but remain favorable toward Israel. He therefore said, “the favor of the One who dwells in the bush”: God should teach you patience as He taught me at the bush.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik calls God’s apparent sleep a condition of concealment while Israel suffers. Mei HaShiloach explains the burning bush as God teaching Moses that He is present with Israel in that very distress and patiently bears the oppressor’s continued existence. The comparison gives content to divine presence during concealment; its scene of Moses learning patience is distinct from Purim’s later awakening to deliverance.

records.themeTitle: Deliverance discloses the purpose of the earlier pressure
records.themeSummary: Chanukah’s rest includes recognizing how the decree awakened resistance.
records.originHebrew: וּבָזֶה הַחֹדֶשׁ הָיָה נֵס חֲנֻכָּה, וְזֶה "הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ בְּשֵׁינָה", שֶׁהַשֵּׁם סוֹמֵךְ לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה נְפִילָה; שֶׁמִּזֶּה הַחֹשֶׁךְ נִצְמַח הַיְשׁוּעָה: שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם הָיוּ גַּם כֵּן תַּחַת מֶמְשַׁלְתָּם, אַךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁגָּזְרוּ גְּזֵרוֹת כָּאֵלּוּ וְהֶחְשִׁיכוּ עֵינֵיהֶם, עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרְרוּ וּמָסְרוּ עַצְמָם עַל זֶה, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֲזָרָם וְנִתְגַּבְּרוּ עֲלֵיהֶם. וְזֶהוּ "סוֹמֵךְ" שֶׁהַנְּפִילָה הִיא צֹרֶךְ עֲלִיָּה;
records.originEnglish: In this month the Chanukah miracle occurred. This is “He made samekh rule over sleep”: God supports all who fall so that it will not become a fall. Deliverance grew from this darkness. Previously they too had been under [Greek] rule, but once decrees of this kind darkened their eyes, they were awakened through them and risked their lives for this. God helped them, and they prevailed. This is “supports”: the fall is needed for an ascent.
records.targetHebrew: וְאָז בִּימֵי הַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים הָיָה לָהֶם הַנְּיָחָא בִּבְחִינַת יִחוּדָא עִלָּאָה, שֶׁהִכִּירוּ הַכֹּל שֶׁהַגְּזֵרָה הָיָה לְטוֹבָתָם, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִצְּחוּ אֶת הַיְּוָנִים וּפָרְקוּ עֻלָּם; שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם הָיוּ מְשֻׁעְבָּדִים לָהֶם וְהֻצְרַךְ שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק לָצֵאת נֶגְדּוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יוֹמָא ס״ט עַמּוּד א׳), וְלוּלֵא הַגְּזֵרוֹת בְּוַדַּאי לֹא הָיוּ קָמִים כְּנֶגְדּוֹ; רַק עַל יְדֵי הַגְּזֵרָה שֶׁרָצוּ לְהַעֲבִירָם עַל דָּת מָסְרוּ עַצְמָם לְמִיתָה לְהִלָּחֵם נֶגְדּוֹ, וְנַעֲשָׂה לָהֶם הַנֵּס וּפָרְקוּ עֻלָּם מֵעַל צַוָּארֵיהֶם, וְזֶהוּ רֶמֶז כ״ה אַתְוָון שֶׁבְּיִחוּדָא עִלָּאָה שֶׁכָּתַב בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר.
records.targetEnglish: Then, in the days of the Hasmoneans, they had rest in the aspect of higher unity. All recognized that the decree had been for their good, because through it they defeated the Greeks and threw off their yoke. Previously they were subject to them, and Simeon the Righteous had to go out to meet [the ruler], as stated in Yoma 69a. Without the decrees they certainly would not have risen against him. Only because of the decree seeking to turn them from their religion were they prepared to die in order to fight him. The miracle was performed for them, and they removed the yoke from their necks. This is the allusion of the twenty-five letters in the higher unification mentioned in Tikkunei Zohar.
records.explanation: The Kislev passage gives the sequence: an already subject people was awakened by the religious decrees, resisted with self-sacrifice, and received divine help. Pri Tzadik’s Chanukah discourse places this same sequence within the meaning of rest and higher unity: after deliverance they could recognize a good that had not been visible within the decree. It adds the attained recognition to the mechanism described here.

records.themeTitle: Opposition can begin a deliverance that service completes
records.themeSummary: The pressure of the enemy and Israel’s response play distinct roles.
records.originHebrew: שֶׁמִּזֶּה הַחֹשֶׁךְ נִצְמַח הַיְשׁוּעָה: שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם הָיוּ גַּם כֵּן תַּחַת מֶמְשַׁלְתָּם, אַךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁגָּזְרוּ גְּזֵרוֹת כָּאֵלּוּ וְהֶחְשִׁיכוּ עֵינֵיהֶם, עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרְרוּ וּמָסְרוּ עַצְמָם עַל זֶה, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֲזָרָם וְנִתְגַּבְּרוּ עֲלֵיהֶם. וְזֶהוּ "סוֹמֵךְ" שֶׁהַנְּפִילָה הִיא צֹרֶךְ עֲלִיָּה;
records.originEnglish: Deliverance grew from this darkness. Previously they too had been under [Greek] rule, but once decrees of this kind darkened their eyes, they were awakened through them and risked their lives for this. God helped them, and they prevailed. This is “supports”: the fall is needed for an ascent.
records.targetRef: Tiferet Yosef, The Seventh Day of Pesach 6
records.targetHebrew: אשר לפעמים התחלת התעוררות הישועה מתחיל כמו שכתיב (דברים ל״ב:כ״ז) לולי כעס אויב אגור פן ינכרו צרימו, פן יאמרו ידינו רמה ולא ד' פעל כל זאת. וכמו שאיתא במדרש (רבה שמות יג) ומי גרם להם שיצאו משם לולי כעס אויב. הרי שמזה נצמח במצרים התחלת התעוררות הישועה. והגם שבתפיסתינו הוא קטן מאד שכל הישועה נצמח בהתחלה מן כעס אויב. מ"מ מאחר שראינו שהשי"ת בחר מן זה היסוד שיוצמח לפעמים מן זה הישועה הוא גדול ככל היסודות. כי מה שהשי"ת בוחר, אין שום נפקא מינה מן דבר גדול לדבר קטן. וזה שאומר המדרש אמר אויב ארדוף אשיג וכו' היה צריך להיות תחילת השירה. היינו שמזה הכעס אויב נצמח כל התעוררות הישועה. רק מאחר שאחר כל זה הציב השי"ת שישראל יברר עצמו על זה, למה באמת בחר בו השי"ת. והגם שההתחלה היה מן כעס אויב, מ"מ אחר כל זה הגמר הישועה הוא מן עבודת ישראל.
records.targetEnglish: The beginning of the awakening of deliverance sometimes comes in the manner of “Were it not that I feared the enemy’s provocation, lest their adversaries misunderstand, lest they say: Our hand is raised, and the Lord did not do all this.” As the Midrash says, what caused them to leave there? The enemy’s provocation. Thus the beginning of deliverance in Egypt grew from this. Although it seems very small to our apprehension that the whole deliverance should initially grow from the enemy’s provocation, since we see that God chose this foundation from which deliverance sometimes grows, it is as great as all foundations. In what God chooses, there is no difference between a great thing and a small one. This is the Midrash’s statement that “The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake…” should have begun the song: from the enemy’s provocation the whole awakening of deliverance grew. Yet afterwards God established that Israel should clarify why He truly chose them. Although the beginning came from the enemy’s provocation, the completion of deliverance nevertheless comes from Israel’s service.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik shows how oppression awakened Israel’s resistance and was followed by divine help. Tiferet Yosef distinguishes the beginning of deliverance through the enemy’s provocation from its completion through Israel’s service. Its account concerns Egypt and the honor of God; the shared structure clarifies why Pri Tzadik includes Israel’s awakened self-sacrifice in the ascent that follows darkness.

records.themeTitle: An ancestor’s strength can support the whole people
records.themeSummary: The shared form of Israel lets a particular victory become a lasting communal capacity.
records.originHebrew: וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר: דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הָאֲוִיר שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ אוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ, וְהַמַּקִּיף רוֹעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שִׁבְעָה רוֹעִים שֶׁהֵם מֶרְכָּבָה לְשֶׁבַע הַמִּדּוֹת. וְכֵן דָּרַשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ: "'סָמֶךְ' זוֹ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וְכוּלֵיהּ", וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁהַפְּנִימִיּוּת הוּא יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וְ"הָרִים סָבִיב לָהּ"; "הָרִים" אֵלּוּ אָבוֹת, קְדֻשַּׁת הָאָבוֹת: דְּאַבְרָהָם קְרָאוֹ "הַר", יִצְחָק "שָׂדֶה", וְיַעֲקֹב קְרָאוֹ "בַּיִת", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳).
records.originEnglish: Afterwards it says that Israel is the air within the letter samekh, and Israel’s shepherds form the surrounding boundary—the seven shepherds who are the vehicle for the seven qualities. So too it expounds, “‘Samekh’ is Jerusalem”: Jerusalem is the interior, with “mountains around her.” The mountains are the patriarchs, the holiness of the patriarchs: Abraham called it a mountain, Isaac a field, and Jacob a house, as the Gemara says.
records.targetHebrew: כַּאֲשֶׁר הָאָדָם גּוֹדֵר עַצְמוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה דָבָר לְהִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגֶד יִצְרוֹ בְּכָל כֹּחוֹ, הוּא גּוֹדֵר בְּכֹחוֹ זֶה כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מֵאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית שֶׁבְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת בְּאוֹתוֹ דָבָר, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ [בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל״ב] וּבְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה [עַל פָּסוּק "גַּן נָעוּל"]: שָׂרָה יָרְדָה לְמִצְרַיִם וְגָדְרָה עַצְמָהּ מִן הָעֶרְוָה וְכָל הַנָּשִׁים נִגְדְּרוּ בִּזְכוּתָהּ, וְיוֹסֵף יָרַד לְמִצְרַיִם וְגָדַר עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֶרְוָה וְנִגְדְּרוּ כָּל הַזְּכָרִים בִּזְכוּתוֹ; וְאִם בְּשָׂרָה יֵשׁ לוֹמַר לְפִי שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִזַּרְעָהּ וְצֶאֱצָאֶיהָ, בְּיוֹסֵף לֹא שַׁיָּךְ זֶה, וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ לְפִי שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹמָה אַחַת, וּבִשְׁלֵמוּת הָאֶחָד נִשְׁלָם כָּל הַקּוֹמָה.
records.targetEnglish: When a person restrains himself in a matter, overcoming his inclination with all his strength, through this power he restrains all the souls of the Jewish people in all generations in that matter. Our sages say: Sarah descended to Egypt and restrained herself from forbidden sexual relations, and all the women were restrained in her merit; Joseph descended to Egypt and restrained himself, and all the males were restrained in his merit. With Sarah one might say this is because all Israel are her offspring and descendants; that cannot be said of Joseph. It must therefore be because all Israel constitute one whole form, and through the perfection of one member the whole form is perfected.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik describes Israel as surrounded by the merit of its fathers and shepherds. Divrei Soferim explains how such merit can act beyond the person who first attained it: the members of Israel constitute one whole, so the restraint of Sarah and Joseph establishes a capacity in others. This gives an inward mechanism for the ancestral support pictured by the enclosing samekh.

records.themeTitle: The patriarchs’ trials leave a protective light
records.themeSummary: A clarity established by the ancestors can awaken against later concealment.
records.originHebrew: דָּבָר אַחֵר: 'סָמֶךְ' אֵלּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁסּוֹמְכִין לָהֶם תָּמִיד זְכוּת אֲבוֹתֵיהֶם: אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק, וְיַעֲקֹב, וְיוֹסֵף, מֹשֶׁה, וְאַהֲרֹן, וְדָוִד, וּשְׁלֹמֹה וְכוּלֵיהּ". וְהַיְנוּ דְּאוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ מוֹרֶה עַל אוֹר מַקִּיף;
records.originEnglish: “Samekh” refers to Israel, who are always supported by the merit of their fathers: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, David, and Solomon. The letter samekh indicates an encompassing light.
records.targetHebrew: כי הנה כל ענין נסיון שהיה אצל האבות הקדושים לא היה נצרך כלל מצדם כי הם היו מבוררים בתכלית השלימות גם בלעדי הנסיונות אלא כל עסק הנסיון שהיה גבי האבות היה רק למען שיהיה נשאר בקביעות לדורי דורות, כשיעמוד לפעמים ח"ו נגד ישראל איזה הסתרה אזי יתעורר נגדה הבהירות מהנסיונות של אבות הקדושים להגן על ישראל
records.targetEnglish: The trials experienced by the holy patriarchs were not needed from their own side, for they were already completely clarified even without the trials. The whole purpose of their trials was that this should remain established for generations: when some concealment should confront Israel, God forbid, the clarity of the holy patriarchs’ trials would awaken against it to protect Israel.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik’s enclosing shepherds signify the enduring support of ancestral merit. Sod Yesharim explains why the patriarchs’ trials matter to descendants: the clarified light remains available when a later concealment confronts Israel. This translates the picture of being surrounded into the particular function of protection during a test.
records.translationProvenance: New English translations of the unchanged canonical Hebrew excerpts, prepared for this editorial connection. The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: Abraham moves from an apparent ending to a beginning
records.themeSummary: The east signifies the emergence of descendants whose source is Abraham.
records.originHebrew: וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁהוּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם סָבַר שֶׁהוּא הַסּוֹף "צֶדֶק", מַלְכוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא, מִדָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה; "מַהְדַּרְנָא וּמוֹקֵמְנָא לֵיהּ בַּמִּזְרָח", שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ יַתְחִיל עִקַּר זְרִיחַת הָאוֹר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: "'יְהִי אוֹר' זֶה אַבְרָהָם". וְיִצְחָק גַּם כֵּן בַּמִּזְרָח, שֶׁהוּא עִקַּר זְרִיחַת הָאוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּמּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה, וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁנּוֹלַד מִתּוֹלָדָה יִשְׂרָאֵל.
records.originEnglish: Abraham our father thought that he was the end: “tzedek,” holy kingship, the last quality. “I will move it and establish it in the east”: from him the principal shining of the light would begin, as Genesis Rabbah says, “‘Let there be light’—this is Abraham.” Isaac too is in the east, for he is the principal dawning of Israel’s light: he was the first circumcised on the eighth day, born an Israelite by birth.
records.targetHebrew: וְעַד שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁלַם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּתַכְלִית שְׁלֵמוּתוֹ, וְלֹא זָכָה עֲדַיִן לְלֵידַת יִצְחָק וְלִהְיוֹת אָב לָאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַהִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת מִמֶּנּוּ, לֹא הָיָה אוֹתוֹ כּוֹכָב מֵאִיר וּמַזְהִיר כְּלָל בַּתְּחִלָּה לִהְיוֹת רֹאשׁ לַכּוֹכָבִים, וְלֹא נִכָּר אוֹרוֹ רַק בְּסוֹף הַלַּיְלָה סָמוּךְ לִשְׁקִיעַת הַלְּבָנָה [כִּי כְּבָר הִתְחִיל לְהָאִיר מִצַּד אוֹר עַצְמוֹ, אֲבָל הָיָה עֲדַיִן בְּתַכְלִית הַקֹּטֶן וְהַהֶעְלֵם], וְזֶהוּ "דְּקָאֵי בְּמַעֲרָב", שֶׁשָּׁם הַלְּבָנָה שׁוֹקַעַת בְּסוֹף הַלַּיְלָה. וּמִזֶּה הֵבִין דְּהוּא עֲרִירִי וְאֵין שׁוּם הִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת נִמְשָׁךְ מִמֶּנּוּ וְאַחֲרָיו; וְאָמַר לוֹ: "מַהְדַּרְנָא לְמִזְרָח", שֶׁהוּא בִּתְחִלַּת הַזְּרִיחָה, דְּאַדְּרַבָּה, אַתָּה רֹאשׁ לְכָל הִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת הָאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית וְרִאשׁוֹן לְכָל הַכּוֹכָבִים. וְזֶה כְּשֶׁנִּשְׁלַם וְזָכָה לְלֵידַת יִצְחָק וְהִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת הָאֻמָּה מִמֶּנּוּ, אָז הִתְחִיל לְהַזְרִיחַ אוֹתוֹ כּוֹכָב מִיָּד בִּתְחִלַּת הַלַּיְלָה בַּמִּזְרָח כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא הַיּוֹם.
records.targetEnglish: Before Abraham our father reached his full perfection and merited Isaac’s birth, becoming the father of the Jewish people from whom its unfolding would proceed, that star did not yet shine at the beginning as the first of the stars. Its light was recognizable only at the night’s end, near the moon’s setting: it had already begun to shine through his own light, but was still exceedingly small and concealed. This is “it stands in the west,” where the moon sets at the night’s end. From this he understood that he was childless and that no further unfolding would proceed from and after him. God told him, “I will move it to the east,” the beginning of the shining: on the contrary, you are the head of the whole unfolding of the Jewish people and the first of all the stars. When he became complete and merited Isaac’s birth and the people’s unfolding from him, that star began to shine at the beginning of the night in the east, as it does today.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik reads the movement of Abraham’s star from west to east as the change from an apparent endpoint into the beginning of Israel’s light. In a reported dream, Divrei Chalomot develops that contrast through the difference between Abraham’s personal illumination and his completed role as the father of an unfolding people. The comparison explains the spiritual meaning of the directions in the author’s reading.

records.themeTitle: The promise can open a new capacity to perceive
records.themeSummary: Abraham trusts that God can change the very limits of his present understanding.
records.originHebrew: וּבַגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קנ״ו עַמּוּד ב׳): "מַה דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּקָאֵי צֶדֶק בַּמַּעֲרָב? מַהְדַּרְנָא וּמוֹקֵמְנָא לֵיהּ בַּמִּזְרָח וְכוּלֵיהּ", וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁהוּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם סָבַר שֶׁהוּא הַסּוֹף "צֶדֶק", מַלְכוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא, מִדָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה; "מַהְדַּרְנָא וּמוֹקֵמְנָא לֵיהּ בַּמִּזְרָח", שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ יַתְחִיל עִקַּר זְרִיחַת הָאוֹר,
records.originEnglish: In the Gemara: “What are you thinking—that Jupiter stands in the west? I will move it and establish it in the east.” Abraham our father thought that he was the end: “tzedek,” holy kingship, the last quality. “I will move it and establish it in the east”: from him the principal shining of the light would begin.
records.targetHebrew: ומצד תפיסתו ראה שאברם אינו מוליד, ואח"כ כשאמר לו הקב"ה מאי דעתך דקאי צדק במערב מהדרנא ומוקמינא ליה במזרח, כמו שאיתא בש"ס (שבת קנו.), ובאם אאע"ה היה מחשב לעצמו אז איזה כח, היה מקום לו לאמר אחד משני דברים, או שלא להאמין יען שבתפיסתו רואה היפך מזה, או היה יכול לומר מה שאני רואה עתה בתפיסתי ג"כ אינו אמת, או מה שחקרתי בתפיסתי מי הוא בעל הבירה עד שבאתי להכרה זו שהשי"ת הוא בעל הבירה גם זה ח"ו אינו אמת. ומזה שהאמין בד' בהבטחה זו, מוכח שאאע"ה לא חשב לעצמו מכל עבודתו שום כח, ואף שלא הבין בתפיסתו איך יתקיים הבטחה זאת, אבל האמין שבכחו ית' ברגע אחת ליתן לו תפיסה אחרת שיכיר בתפיסתו שיוכל להוליד.
records.targetEnglish: From his present apprehension Abraham saw that Abram could not beget. Afterwards the Holy One said, “What are you thinking—that Jupiter stands in the west? I will move it and establish it in the east,” as the Talmud states. Had Abraham then ascribed some power to himself, he could have taken one of two approaches: refuse to believe because he perceived the opposite, or say that what he now perceived was untrue—or that his earlier inquiry into who owned the palace, through which he recognized God as its owner, was also, God forbid, untrue. His belief in this divine promise proves that Abraham ascribed no independent power to himself from all his work. Although he did not understand how the promise would be fulfilled, he trusted that God could give him a different apprehension in a moment, through which he would recognize that he could beget.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik describes Abraham as thinking he was the end and God establishing him as a beginning. Tiferet Yosef explains the same talmudic promise through Abraham’s relationship to his own understanding: he does not make his current perception of barrenness the limit of what God can reveal. The target clarifies the trust involved in moving from the apparent endpoint toward fatherhood.
records.translationProvenance: New English translations of the unchanged canonical Hebrew excerpts, prepared for this editorial connection. The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: The hidden good becomes receivable through measure
records.themeSummary: The north’s stored reward is explained through the strength that brings kindness into human reach.
records.originHebrew: וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם נִתְנַבְּאוּ עַל הָאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּגְנַז לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, וְזֶהוּ "אֲשֶׁר צָפַנְתָּ לִּירֵאֶיךָ". וְלֶעָתִיד כְּתִיב: "אֹמַר לַצָּפוֹן תֵּנִי וְגוֹמֵר", וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג׳ קע״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): "לְזִמְנָא דְּאָתֵי קָרֵי קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְצָפוֹן וְיֵימָא לֵיהּ: בָּךְ יְהִיבַת כָּל טִיבוּ וְכָל אַגְרָא טָב לִבְנַי וְכוּלֵיהּ", וְהַיְנוּ אוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן הַנִּגְנָז לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא.
records.originEnglish: Both [David and Solomon] prophesied about the first light, which was hidden away for the righteous in the future. This is “which You have stored for those who fear You.” Concerning the future it is written, “I will say to the north, ‘Give!’.” The Zohar says that in the future the Holy One will call to the north and say, “In you I placed every good and every good reward for My children.” This is the first light hidden away for the righteous in the future.
records.targetHebrew: וזהו דאיתא בזוה"ק (שלח קעג:) אומר לצפון תני וגו' בך יהבית כל טיבו. והיכן גנזו הקב"ה בצמצומים של יצחק ועל זה רומז צפון וכמבואר שם לזמנא דאתי קרי קב"ה לצפון ויימא ליה בך יהבית כל טיבו וכל אגר טב לבני דסבלו כמה בישין בהאי עלמא על קדושת שמי הב אגרין טבין דיהבית בך הה"ד אומר לצפון תני וגו' והיינו אשר צפנת ליראיך וגו' כי מצד השי"ת שהוא רב חסד מתפשט החסד ומרחיב והולך עד בלי די ומהתפשטות כזה בלי צמצום ממדת הגבורה יכול להתבטל כל הבריאה כדאיתא בספר יצירה כשירוץ לבך שוב לאחד היינו שיכול להתבטל באחדותו ית' וכדאיתא בזוה"ק (ויקרא ה.) גדול ה' ומהולל מאד תושבחתא דא בשני ולא בראשון כי אימתי אקרי קב"ה גדול בשעתא דכנסת ישראל בהדיה. וזה בשני דוקא שמורה על מדת הגבורה שהיא כלי המגביל את החסד למען שיהיה הכרה בו
records.targetEnglish: This is the Zohar’s teaching, “I will say to the north, ‘Give!’”: “In you I placed every good.” Where did the Holy One hide it? In Isaac’s limitations; this is what the north signifies. As it explains: in the future the Holy One will call to the north and say, “In you I placed every good and every good reward for My children who endured many hardships in this world for the sanctification of My name. Give the good rewards I placed in you.” This is “which You have stored for those who fear You.” For from God’s side, in His abundant kindness, kindness spreads and expands without limit; such expansion without the restraint of strength could nullify the whole creation. Thus Sefer Yetzirah says, “If your heart runs, return to the One”: one can be nullified in His unity. The Zohar therefore explains that “Great is the Lord and greatly praised” is the praise of the second [day], not the first: when is the Holy One called great? When the community of Israel is with Him. This is specifically the second day, which signifies the quality of strength, which is the vessel limiting kindness so that there can be recognition of it.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik identifies the north with the light and reward stored for the righteous. Sod Yesharim develops the same “I will say to the north, ‘Give!’” teaching by explaining that unbounded kindness needs a limiting vessel to become recognizable and receivable by a creature. Its discussion assigns this work to Isaac’s strength, while Pri Tzadik here speaks of David and Solomon as prophets of the stored reward; the comparison preserves those different assignments.
records.translationProvenance: New English translations of the unchanged canonical Hebrew excerpts, prepared for this editorial connection. The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: A later awakening can raise earlier permitted activity
records.themeSummary: Life directed toward Heaven can repair the spiritual sleep of ordinary conduct.
records.originHebrew: וְשֵׁם כִּסְלֵו הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִהְיֶה בְכִסְלֶךָ וְשָׁמַר רַגְלְךָ מִלָּכֶד", וּפֵרֵשׁ רַשְׁיִ" מִירוּשַׁלְמִי: "בִּדְבָרִים שֶׁאַתָּה כְּסִיל בָּהֶם"; וְהַיְנוּ אַף בְּשֵׁינָה, אַף כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם הוֹלֵךְ בָּטֵל, דְּיוֹשֵׁב בָּטֵל כְּיָשֵׁן דָּמֵי, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה י״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): "'אֵלֵךְ וְאֶתְגָּרֶה בְּשֵׁינָה', תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: 'וּבְתוֹרָתוֹ יֶהְגֶּה וְגוֹמֵר'", וְהַיְנוּ דְּשֵׁינָה הוּא כְּשֶׁהוֹלֵךְ בָּטֵל.
records.originEnglish: The name Kislev follows the verse, “For the Lord will be your confidence and will guard your foot from being caught.” Rashi, from the Jerusalem Talmud, explains: in matters in which you are foolish. This means even in sleep, even when a person goes about idly, for sitting idle is like sleeping. As the Gemara says, might one say, “I will go and provoke sleep”? Scripture says, “In His Torah he shall meditate.” Sleep here means going about idly.
records.targetHebrew: וְכֵן כָּל שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר פַּעַם אַחַת יוּכַל לְהַעֲלוֹת כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁל הֶתֵּר וְדִבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת שֶׁעָשָׂה (וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוֹת בְּלֹא כַּוָּנָה וְחִיּוּת) מִקֹּדֶם, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ פַּעַם אַחֶרֶת עִם חִיּוּת וְכַוָּנָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם. וּבְיוֹתֵר בַּאֲכִילָה שֶׁהִיא דֻּגְמַת הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת (שֶׁבָּהֶם נוֹהֵג דִּין הַגְּרִירָה כִּדְאִיתָא בְּשַׁבָּת), וַאֲכִילָה גּוֹרֶרֶת אֲכִילָה לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹתָהּ.
records.targetEnglish: Likewise, whenever a person awakens even once, he can raise all the permitted deeds and optional activities he did previously—and certainly commandments performed without intention and vitality—by performing that activity another time with vitality and intention for the sake of Heaven. This applies especially to eating, which resembles the offerings, where the rule of one item drawing another after it applies, as stated in Shabbat: one act of eating draws another after it to become like it.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik includes idle, inattentive life within the image of sleep that can receive divine support. Et HaOchel describes one way an awakening can repair that condition: performing a permitted activity with fresh intention can raise the earlier instances of it. Its express restriction to permitted and optional acts is retained, as is the need for an actual new act with vitality and intention.

records.themeTitle: An inherited holiness can reach the organs of action
records.themeSummary: The fathers’ established holiness supplies a capacity that a person trains into daily conduct.
records.originHebrew: וְכֵן סָמֶ״ךְ אֵלּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁמֻּקָּפִים מֵהַסַּיְעָתוֹת מֵהַשִּׁבְעָה רוֹעִים שֶׁהֵם מֶרְכָּבָה לְשֶׁבַע הַמִּדּוֹת עִם הֵ"א עִלָּאָה, בִּינָה, וְהוּא דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהֵקִים עֻלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ; וְזֶה קְדֻשַּׁת הַחֹדֶשׁ.
records.originEnglish: So too samekh refers to Israel, surrounded by the assistance of the seven shepherds, who are the vehicle for the seven qualities, together with the upper heh, understanding. This is King David, who established the yoke of repentance, as we said. This is the holiness of the month.
records.targetRef: Tiferet Yosef, Shabbat Chol HaMoed Sukkot 1
records.targetHebrew: אשר אדם בעבודתו צריך להרגיל עצמו בעבודה על כל אברי פעולותיו, שכל אבריו ירגישו מהקדושה, שאפילו הרגל שהוא רחוק מן המחשבה שבראש, יכניס בו ג"כ קדושה מהמחשבה שבראש, שבהגיעו חוץ לתחום ירגיש הרגל בעצמו שעד פה היה רצונו ית' לילך ולא יותר. וזה אם תשיב משבת רגלך, וכעין דאיתא בירושלמי (ברכות פרק ב') בואו ונחזיק טיבותא לרישא דכד מטי למודים מגרמיה קא כרע. ובאמת עיקר כח האדם, שיכול להכניס קדושתו על כל פעולותיו, נמשך הכל יען אשר נשרש בו קדושה בקביעות משורש קדושת אבות, ומזה הכח קדושה יכול להכניס גם בכלי פעולותיו,
records.targetEnglish: A person must train himself in service throughout all his organs of action, so that all his limbs feel holiness. Even the foot, which is far from the thought in the head, should receive holiness from that thought: upon reaching the boundary, the foot itself should sense that God’s will was to walk this far and no farther. This is “If you turn back your foot because of Shabbat.” It resembles the Jerusalem Talmud’s statement, “Let us give thanks to the head, for when it reaches Modim it bows of itself.” In truth, a person’s whole power to bring holiness into all his actions flows from the holiness permanently rooted within him from the patriarchs’ holiness. From that holy power he can bring holiness into the organs of action as well.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik names the surrounding help of the shepherds as part of Kislev’s holiness. Tiferet Yosef explains how holiness rooted in the fathers can support a person’s practical faculties: deliberate habituation brings it even into a limb far from conscious thought. It develops the movement from inherited support to embodied service.

records.themeTitle: Received light can disclose a depth beyond direct brilliance
records.themeSummary: The fiftieth gate is approached through Oral Torah without diminishing Moses’ unique degree.
records.originHebrew: וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּסוֹף הַחֹדֶשׁ זוֹכִין לָאוֹר, נְהוֹרָא עִלָּאָה, הָאוֹר "כִּי טוֹב", וּבוֹ נֵס חֲנֻכָּה; וְאָז יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמַּקִּיף, שֶׁנַּעֲשִׂים כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַסָּמֶ״ךְ, בִּינָה, שֶׁמַּקִּיפִים לְהָאוֹר חָכְמָה, וְהוּא "מְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין שֶׁאֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים עוֹמְדִים שָׁם" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרָכוֹת ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳), וְהִיא שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים מֵחֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה;
records.originEnglish: At the end of the month they merit light—the supernal light called “good”—and in it is the Chanukah miracle. Israel then becomes the surrounding circle: the community of Israel becomes samekh, understanding, encompassing the light of wisdom. This is “the place where penitents stand, where completely righteous people do not stand,” and it is the fiftieth gate of the fifty gates of understanding.
records.targetHebrew: וְיָדוּעַ דִּבְכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ מ״ט פָּנִים טָהוֹר וְטָמֵא, שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד ז׳ יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כָּל אַחַת כָּלוּל מִזַּיִ״ן וְשַׁעַר הַנּוּ״ן הַנֶּעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, הוּא מַה שֶּׁחוֹזֵר הַכֹּל לַמָּקוֹר לִהְיוֹת כּוּלּוֹ טָהוֹר וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה ״פְּנֵי חַמָּה״ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ע״ה עַמּוּד א׳) בְּהַשָּׂגַת עֶצֶם הָאוֹר הַמֵּאִיר, לֹא יָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג אוֹר דְּשַׁעַר הַזֶּה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֲבָל עַל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אָמְרוּ [בִּמְנָחוֹת כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳ וּבְוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ״ב] שֶׁנִּגְלָה לוֹ מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִגְלָה לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּפֵירֵשׁ בְּ״מְגַלֵּה עֲמוּקוֹת״ שֶׁנִּגְלָה לוֹ שַׁעַר הַנּוּ״ן הַנֶּעְלָם מִמֹּשֶׁה וְלֹא שֶׁהָיָה מַעֲלָתוֹ גְּדוֹלָה מִמֶּנּוּ, שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר וְ״לֹא קָם [נָבִיא עוֹד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל] כְּמֹשֶׁה״ (דְּבָרִים ל״ד:י׳) אֲבָל לְפִי שֶׁהַשָּׂגָתוֹ הוּא מֵאוֹר הַלְּבָנָה הַמְקַבֵּל מֵאוֹר הַחַמָּה, כִּי הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַמְקַבֵּל מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְהִיא הַשָּׂגַת הַחָכְמָה דְּחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל זֶה [בָּבָא בַּתְרָא י״ב עַמּוּד א׳] דְּ״עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא״ הַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג יוֹתֵר עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהַשָּׂגָתוֹ בְּאוֹר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַבְהִיק וּמַבְרִיק כָּל כָּךְ
records.targetEnglish: In every matter there are forty-nine aspects of purity and impurity, corresponding to the seven days of this world’s structure, each comprising seven. The fiftieth gate, hidden in this world, is where everything returns to its source to become wholly pure. Moses our teacher, whose face was like the sun in apprehending the very illuminating light, could not apprehend this gate’s light in this world. Yet our sages say of Rabbi Akiva that something was revealed to him that was not revealed to Moses; Megalleh Amukkot explains this as the fiftieth gate hidden from Moses. This does not mean that his degree was greater than Moses’, which is impossible, for “No prophet arose again in Israel like Moses.” Rather, his apprehension was through the moon’s light, receiving from the sun: he is the root of Oral Torah, which receives from Written Torah. This is the wisdom of Israel’s sages, of which it is said that a sage surpasses a prophet: he can apprehend more because his apprehension is in a light that is not so intensely bright and flashing.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik joins the fiftieth gate, the superiority attained through repentance, and the gift of Oral Torah. Takanat HaShavin explains why the receiving mode of Oral Torah can disclose a depth unavailable through direct solar brilliance. It expressly preserves Moses’ unique greatness even when describing Rabbi Akiva’s additional attainment, helping clarify the relation between higher and lower wisdom here.

records.themeTitle: The fiftieth gate reveals the unity of the many qualities
records.themeSummary: Work within distinct qualities prepares for a disclosure of their common root.
records.originHebrew: וְאָז יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמַּקִּיף, שֶׁנַּעֲשִׂים כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַסָּמֶ״ךְ, בִּינָה, שֶׁמַּקִּיפִים לְהָאוֹר חָכְמָה, וְהוּא "מְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין שֶׁאֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים עוֹמְדִים שָׁם" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרָכוֹת ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳), וְהִיא שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים מֵחֲמִשִּׁים שַׁעֲרֵי בִינָה;
records.originEnglish: Israel then becomes the surrounding circle: the community of Israel becomes samekh, understanding, encompassing the light of wisdom. This is “the place where penitents stand, where completely righteous people do not stand,” and it is the fiftieth gate of the fifty gates of understanding.
records.targetRef: Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 54:1
records.targetHebrew: ולכן אחר יציאת מצרים שהתחילו ישראל לברר בבחירתם כל המ"ט מדות והמדות כמו שהם נפרדים לפרטים בפני עצמם המה משוללי שלימות לכך נצטוו לספור מ"ט יום עד שמגיעים ליום חמשים ואז מנהיר משער הנו"ן להכיר האחדות מהשורש בכל המדות ואותה ההכרה נקרא תורה כמבואר בזוה"ק (מצורע נ"ג:) מאי תורה דאורי וגלי מה דהוו סתים בקדמיתא ולא אתידע:
records.targetEnglish: Therefore, after the exodus from Egypt, when Israel began to clarify all forty-nine qualities through their choice, the qualities considered as separate particulars were still without completeness. They were commanded to count forty-nine days until reaching the fiftieth day. The fiftieth gate then shines, making recognizable the root’s unity within all the qualities. That recognition is called Torah, as the Zohar explains: what is Torah? That which teaches and reveals what was previously concealed and unknown.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik names the fiftieth gate as the encompassing understanding attained at the month’s light and still calls for effort toward Oral Torah. Sod Yesharim explains what the encompassing gate discloses: the separately refined qualities are recognized as one at their root. Its omer sequence supplies a concrete relation between prior work and the subsequent gift of unifying recognition.
records.translationProvenance: New English translations of the unchanged canonical Hebrew excerpts, prepared for this editorial connection. The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: Anger’s corrective role depends on what it confronts
records.themeSummary: The distinction is between anger itself and a narrowly directed response governed by Torah.
records.originHebrew: וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין: הָא כַּעַס מִדָּה מְגֻנָּה, כְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי כַעַס בְּחֵיק כְּסִילִים יָנוּחַ", וּכְתִיב: "כִּי בְּרֹב חָכְמָה רָב כָּעַס", וְהֵיאַךְ שַׁיָּךְ שֶׁנִּבְרָא חֹדֶשׁ כִּסְלֵו בְּרֹגֶז שֶׁהוּא כַּעַס? וְכֵן קָשֶׁה בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ס״א עַמּוּד ב׳): "כָּבֵד כּוֹעֵס", וְהוּא אֵבֶר שֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְאֵיךְ נִבְרָא אֵבֶר מְיֻחָד לְכַעַס?
records.originEnglish: It needs explanation: anger is a disgraceful quality, as it is said, “Anger rests in the bosom of fools,” and “With much wisdom comes much anger.” How can the month of Kislev have been created through agitation, which is anger? The same question applies to “the liver becomes angry”: it is an organ God created—how was an organ specifically for anger created?
records.targetHebrew: וְאֵין בּוֹ טוֹב כְּלָל, רַק לְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, הַיְינוּ חַיָּבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין, וְהוּא רִתְחָא דְּרַבָּנַן דְּטָב [תַּעֲנִית ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳]. וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן רַק מִצַּד שֶׁנִּמְצָא כְּסִילוּת בָּעוֹלָם, דְּלוּלֵי כֵן אֵין מָקוֹם לְרִתְחָא, וּמִצַּד הַחָכְמָה אֵין בּוֹ צַד טוֹב וְרָאוּי כְּלָל, וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא "כְּסִיל" לְעוֹלָם.
records.targetEnglish: There is no good in it at all except for Torah scholars—that is, [in judging] those liable to the court’s death penalties in the Sanhedrin. This is the beneficial anger of the sages. Even this is only because foolishness exists in the world; without it there would be no place for anger. From the side of wisdom, anger has no good or fitting aspect at all, and it is therefore always called foolish.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik asks why a power identified with the condemned quality of anger was created at all. Sichat Shedim distinguishes anger in itself from its limited corrective use in the presence of wrongdoing, using the Torah court as its example. This helps define the problem answered by the next Kislev paragraph’s holy fire: force is directed at what requires correction, rather than treated as an independent virtue.
records.translationProvenance: New English translations of the unchanged canonical Hebrew excerpts, prepared for this editorial connection. The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: The fire of Torah remains governed by mercy
records.themeSummary: Its necessity comes from Torah, while the person continues to seek grounds for compassion.
records.originHebrew: וְהָעִנְיָן, דְּבֶאֱמֶת שֹׁרֶשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוּא אֵשׁ כַּעַס, וּכְמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַחֲמָתוֹ בָּעֲרָה בוֹ", וְרוֹצֶה לִשְׂרֹף וּלְכַלּוֹת הַכֹּל; אֲבָל לְעֻמַּת זֶה יֵשׁ בִּקְדֻשָּׁה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה לְתַקֵּן הַרְבֵּה כַּעַס, וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן אֵשׁ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תַּעֲנִית ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳): "הַאי צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנַן דְּרָתַח אוֹרַיְּתָא הוּא דְּקָא מַרְתְּחָא לֵיהּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'הֲלוֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ'"; וְהוּא אֵשׁ אוֹכְלָה אֵשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁשּׂוֹרֵף וּמְכַלֶּה אֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע; וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב׳ קפ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳): "רוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנַן טָב אִיהוּ לְכָל סִטְרִין וְכוּלֵיהּ".
records.originEnglish: The root of the evil inclination is the fire of anger, as in “His fury burned within him”; it wishes to burn and consume everything. Corresponding to this in holiness is Oral Torah: much wisdom to repair much anger. It too is fire, as the Gemara says: “When a Torah scholar grows heated, Torah is what heats him, as it is written, ‘Are not My words like fire?’” It is a fire consuming the fire of the evil inclination, burning and consuming that inclination. This is why the Zohar says, “The anger of the sages is good on every side.”
records.targetHebrew: וְרוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנָן טָב בְּכָל סִטְרִין כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קפב עַמּוּד ב), וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַעֲנִית (ד.): דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּקָא מְרַתְּחָא, פֵּירוּשׁ: כְּשֶׁהַכַּעַס הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁהַתּוֹרָה מַרְתִּיחָתוֹ, שֶׁעַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה רָאוּי לִכְעוֹס, כְּעִנְיַן הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין שֶׁדָּנוּ נְפָשׁוֹת, וְאֵין מְמַנִּין בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין זָקֵן וְכוּלֵי (סַנְהֶדְרִין לו:), שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ מְלֵאִים רַחֲמִים בֶּאֱמֶת וּמִשְׁתַּדְּלִים לִמְצוֹא זְכוּת עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה, וּרְתִיחָתָם רַק מִצַּד הֶכְרֵחַ הַתּוֹרָה זֶה נִקְרָא רוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנָן, הָאוֹהֲבֵי הַתּוֹרָה בֶּאֱמֶת, שֶׁגַּם בְּעֵת כַּעֲסוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה וְזוֹכֵר וּמִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּרַחֲמִים. וְהָעֲצִירָה בְּעֵת הַכַּעַס הוּא אַהֲבָה "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ",
records.targetEnglish: “The anger of the sages is good on every side,” as the Zohar says. This is the Gemara’s statement that Torah is what heats him: the anger is only what Torah causes, when according to Torah it is fitting to become angry. The example is the Sanhedrin judging capital cases, concerning which it says that an elderly person is not appointed to the Sanhedrin. They were truly full of mercy and strove to find grounds for acquittal according to Torah; their heat came only from Torah’s necessity. This is called the anger of sages who truly love Torah: even during anger it is only on Torah’s account, and they remember and strive for mercy. Restraint at the time of anger is love “with all your soul.”
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik distinguishes Torah’s holy fire from the destructive fire of the inclination. Tzidkat HaTzadik gives a stringent test for the phrase “the anger of the sages”: it comes only from what Torah requires, while the person continues to remember mercy and seek a favorable judgment. This supplies a concrete criterion for the holy fire described here.

records.themeTitle: A harmful force can yield firmness for service
records.themeSummary: Torah governs the use of intensity instead of surrendering to crookedness.
records.originHebrew: אֲבָל לְעֻמַּת זֶה יֵשׁ בִּקְדֻשָּׁה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה לְתַקֵּן הַרְבֵּה כַּעַס, וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן אֵשׁ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תַּעֲנִית ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳): "הַאי צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנַן דְּרָתַח אוֹרַיְּתָא הוּא דְּקָא מַרְתְּחָא לֵיהּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'הֲלוֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ'"; וְהוּא אֵשׁ אוֹכְלָה אֵשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁשּׂוֹרֵף וּמְכַלֶּה אֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע;
records.originEnglish: Corresponding to this in holiness is Oral Torah: much wisdom to repair much anger. It too is fire, as the Gemara says: “When a Torah scholar grows heated, Torah is what heats him, as it is written, ‘Are not My words like fire?’” It is a fire consuming the fire of the evil inclination, burning and consuming that inclination.
records.targetHebrew: דרך נחש עלי צור, נחש מרמז, אשר אף שמראה גוון טוב אבל הוא משורש עקשות ועקמימות, וזה דרך נחש עלי צור, אשר תקיפות לעבודה יכול אדם לקבל מזה ג"כ, כי מצינו רוגזא דרבנן טב הוא מכל סטרין, כי אף שאיתא בזוה"ק (בראשית כז) כל הכועס כאילו עובד ע"ז, ומ"מ מצינו בש"ס (תענית ד) האי צורבא מרבנן דרתח אורייתא הוא דקא מרתחא ליה, והיינו, כי תקיפות לעבודה יכול אדם לקבל מזה ג"כ.
records.targetEnglish: “The way of a serpent upon a rock”: a serpent signifies that even when it displays a good appearance, its root is stubbornness and crookedness. Yet “the way of a serpent upon a rock” means that a person can receive firmness for service from this as well. We find that the anger of the sages is good on every side. Although the Zohar says that anyone who becomes angry is as though he worshipped idolatry, we nevertheless find in the Talmud: “When a Torah scholar grows heated, Torah is what heats him.” That is, one can receive firmness for service from this too.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik’s consuming fire is a holy use of intensity against the inclination’s destructive fire. Tiferet Yosef explains the same talmudic contrast through “the way of a serpent upon a rock”: even a force rooted in stubborn crookedness can supply firmness for divine service. The target retains the condemnation of ordinary anger beside the limited Torah-directed possibility.
