records.themeTitle: The circle signifies completion of attachment
records.themeSummary: The absence of a head and end concerns a common completeness, while the origin retains earned degrees.
records.originHebrew: וְאוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ מוֹרֶה כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד שֶׁיִּשְׁחֹט הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיֵצֶר הָרָע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סֻכָּה נ״ב עַמּוּד א׳), וְאָז יַעֲשֶׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָחוֹל לַצַּדִּיקִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוֹף תַּעֲנִית ל״א עַמּוּד א׳); וְהַיְנוּ בְּלֹא חִלּוּק מַדְרֵגוֹת כְּמוֹ כָּל דָּבָר עָגֹל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ רֹאשׁ וָסוֹף; וְאַף שֶׁאָז יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן מַדְרֵגוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוֹף בְּרָכוֹת ס״ד עַמּוּד א׳): "תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֵין לָהֶם מְנוּחָה לֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'יֵלְכוּ מֵחַיִל אֶל חָיִל וְגוֹמֵר'", וְיַעֲלוּ בְּכָל פַּעַם מִמַּדְרֵגָה לְמַדְרֵגָה; מִכָּל מָקוֹם כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע, שׁוּב לֹא יִהְיוּ הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת מֵעֲבוֹדָה חֲדָשָׁה, רַק הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת יִהְיוּ מֵהָעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
records.originEnglish: Samekh indicates the future, when the Holy One will slaughter the evil inclination. He will then make a circle for the righteous, as stated at the end of Taanit: without differences of degree, like anything round, which has no head or end. Although there will also be degrees then, as it says, “Torah scholars have no rest, either in this world or in the World to Come,” and they will ascend continually from strength to strength, since there will be no evil inclination the degrees will no longer come from new work; they will come from the work done in this world.
records.targetHebrew: וּכְמוֹ לֶעָתִיד יַעֲשֶׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָחוֹל לַצַּדִּיקִים וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סוֹף תַּעֲנִית לא.), פֵּירוּשׁ עִיגּוּל, דְּיִתְגַּלֶּה מַדְרֵגַת הָעִיגּוּלִים דְּשָׁם אֵין מַדְרֵגוֹת דְּכֻלּוֹ שָׁוֶה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת. מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן קוֹמַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא קוֹמַת הַיּוֹשֶׁר דְּצוּרַת אָדָם, שֶׁבָּזֶה יֵשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת רֹאשׁ וְסוֹף וּקְצוֹת כַּנּוֹדָע, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִנָּצֵל דְּהַיְינוּ לְהַגִּיעַ לִשְׁלֵימוּת גָּמוּר, כִּי כֹּחַ זֶה עֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת כַּנִּזְכָּר עַד בִּיאַת מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁהוּא יִהְיֶה בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת. וּכְפַרְנָס כֵּן דּוֹר (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עֲרָכִין יז.), כָּל הַדּוֹר יִהְיֶה בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת וְאָז יִנָּצְלוּ גַּם מֵעִיּוּן תְּפִלָּה דְּיִהְיֶה דְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר,
records.targetEnglish: In the future the Holy One will make a circle for the righteous. That is, a circle: the degree of the circles will be revealed, where there are no degrees because all is equally complete. Jacob’s form, by contrast, is the upright form of the human being, which has degrees—head, end, and extremities. It is impossible to be entirely free [of the deficiency in attachment discussed here], that is, to reach complete perfection, because this power is not yet complete until the coming of the Messiah, who will be completely perfected. As the leader, so the generation: the whole generation will then be completely perfected, freed of the deficiency in prayer, with complete attachment.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik explains the future circle and immediately qualifies it: ascent in degrees remains, but it grows from work already done in this world. Resisei Layla develops the circle as complete attachment, contrasting it with the differentiated head, ends, and limbs of an upright form. This clarifies the kind of common completeness symbolized by the circle; Pri Tzadik’s further qualification about earned degrees remains explicit in the quoted origin.

The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: This world is the place of new refinement
records.themeSummary: The future completion differs from the present opportunity to acquire through choice.
records.originHebrew: וְאַף שֶׁאָז יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן מַדְרֵגוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוֹף בְּרָכוֹת ס״ד עַמּוּד א׳): "תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֵין לָהֶם מְנוּחָה לֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'יֵלְכוּ מֵחַיִל אֶל חָיִל וְגוֹמֵר'", וְיַעֲלוּ בְּכָל פַּעַם מִמַּדְרֵגָה לְמַדְרֵגָה; מִכָּל מָקוֹם כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע, שׁוּב לֹא יִהְיוּ הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת מֵעֲבוֹדָה חֲדָשָׁה, רַק הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת יִהְיוּ מֵהָעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
records.originEnglish: Although there will also be degrees then, as the Gemara says, “Torah scholars have no rest, either in this world or in the World to Come,” and they will continually ascend from one degree to another, there will no longer be degrees from new work, since there will be no evil inclination. The degrees will come from the work done in this world.
records.targetHebrew: מה שאין כן בהבירור של תחיית המתים שאז יהיה הגמר והסוף שעליו נאמר אלה יעמדו לחיי עולם ואלה יעמדו לחרפה ולדראון עולם היינו שיתפרד אז הרע מן הטוב לגמרי ושוב לא יהיה אילנא דספיקא כי אז יגמרו כל תכלית הבירורין ומה שיפול לחוץ שוב לא יהיה לזאת שום תקומה לכן הבירור של עוה"ז הנקרא יום גשמים הוא גדול יותר שהוא בזמן אילנא דספיקא שיכולין להרויח בו כל פעם חדשות משא"כ בתחיית המתים
records.targetEnglish: In the refinement of resurrection there will be the conclusion and end: “These will stand for everlasting life, and these for shame and everlasting abhorrence.” Evil will then be entirely separated from good; there will no longer be the tree of uncertainty, for the whole purpose of the refinements will be complete. What falls outside then will have no further restoration. The refinement of this world, called the day of rain, is therefore greater: during the time of the tree of uncertainty one can acquire something new each time, which is not so at resurrection.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik distinguishes continued future ascent from acquiring degrees through new work. Sod Yesharim makes a closely related distinction between the present “day of rain,” when further good can still be extracted and acquired, and resurrection as the completion of refinement. The comparison explains why the disappearance of the present uncertainty changes the kind of growth that is possible.

The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: Wisdom renewed in the heart remains joined to its source
records.themeSummary: Oral Torah is humanly apprehended while recognized as God’s wisdom.
records.originHebrew: וְהוּא "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" נֶגֶד חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִתְחַדֵּשׁ בְּלֵב חֲכָמִים, אֲשֶׁר מוֹפִיעַ בְּלִבָּם דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים מִטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא;
records.originEnglish: This stands opposite the holy wisdom of Oral Torah, which is likewise renewed in the hearts of the sages: living words of God shine in their hearts from the dew of the Ancient One.
records.targetHebrew: וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם — מִדַּת מַלְכוּת, סִטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא וּפֶה, וְ״תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה״ קָרֵינַן לָהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמַאֲמַר ״פָּתַח אֵלִיָּהוּ״, כִּי הִיא הַחָכְמָה הַמִּתְחַדֶּשֶׁת בִּלְבָבוֹת דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל. וְעַל כֵּן הִמְשִׁיל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ, עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, חָכְמָתוֹ לְאִשָּׁה. וְאֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל, גַּם זֶה נִקְרָא ״תּוֹרָה״, מֵאַחַר דְּמַכִּירִים שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְגַם חָכְמָתָם הוּא חָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. אֲבָל אֵצֶל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן חָכְמָה, וּמְבָרְכִין עַל חַכְמֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם: ״שֶׁנָּתַן מֵחָכְמָתוֹ״, וּפֵרוּשׁוֹ קַמָּאֵי, שֶׁאֶצְלָם הוּא בִּנְתִינָה, מַה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן אֵצֶל חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: ״שֶׁחָלַק״ וְגוֹמֵר, כִּי ״חֵלֶק הַשֵּׁם עִמּוֹ״, וּכְמוֹ הַחֵלֶק הַדָּבוּק בַּכֹּל (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה, פָּרָשָׁה ב׳, ט׳). וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: ״יֵשׁ חָכְמָה בְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת — תַּאֲמִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ׳וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם׳; תּוֹרָה — אַל תַּאֲמִין״; כִּי חָכְמָתָם אֵינָהּ קְרוּיָה תּוֹרָה כְּלַל, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהִיא נִפְרֶדֶת מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
records.targetEnglish: King Solomon represents kingship, the feminine, receiving side and the mouth, called Oral Torah in the teaching Patach Eliyahu: it is the wisdom renewed in the hearts of the community of Israel. Solomon therefore compared his wisdom to a woman. Among Israel this too is called Torah, since they recognize that everything is from God and that their wisdom too is God’s wisdom. Other nations also possess wisdom, and over their sages one blesses “Who has given of His wisdom.” Earlier authorities explain that with them it is a giving, whereas over Israel’s sages one says “Who has shared”: “The Lord’s portion is His people,” like a part joined to the whole. Our sages say that if one is told there is wisdom among the nations, believe it, as it is said, “I will destroy wise men from Edom”; but if one is told there is Torah, do not believe it. Their wisdom is not called Torah, because it is separate from God.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik distinguishes Greek intellectual wisdom from Oral Torah, even though both involve thought arising in a human mind. Resisei Layla explains the positive distinction: the renewed wisdom of Israel’s heart is called Torah because its source remains recognized as God. The comparison clarifies the relation of human understanding to divine source, rather than resting on the historical opposition alone.

records.themeTitle: The receiving wisdom makes the root accessible through work
records.themeSummary: Solomon’s garments of understanding allow another person to recognize the deeper connection.
records.originHebrew: וְהוּא "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" נֶגֶד חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִתְחַדֵּשׁ בְּלֵב חֲכָמִים, אֲשֶׁר מוֹפִיעַ בְּלִבָּם דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים מִטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא;
records.originEnglish: This stands opposite the holy wisdom of Oral Torah, which is likewise renewed in the hearts of the sages: living words of God shine in their hearts from the dew of the Ancient One.
records.targetHebrew: וביאר אזמו"ר הגה"ק זצל"ה שחכמת שלמה הי' לבוש לחכמת משה רבינו כי חכמת מ"ר הי' להסתכל בעומק ולראות איך שישראל נקשרים בשורש העליון ית' וחכמת שלמה המלך הי' להחכים גם לזולתו ע"י שהולבש זה העומק בלבושים וע"י עבודה באלו הלבושים יכיר האדם את התקשרתו בשורש העליון ית':
records.targetEnglish: My holy grandfather explained that Solomon’s wisdom was a garment for Moses’ wisdom. Moses’ wisdom was to look into the depth and see how Israel is bound to the upper root. King Solomon’s wisdom was to make another person wise as well, by clothing this depth in garments. Through work within those garments, a person would recognize his own connection to the upper root.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik describes Oral Torah as divine words renewed within the sages’ hearts. Sod Yesharim explains the receiving relation through Solomon and Moses: the deeper recognition is clothed so that another person, working through those forms, can apprehend the connection to the upper root. This develops the positive work of the humanly articulated wisdom that Pri Tzadik contrasts with Greek philosophy.

records.themeTitle: Awe tests the quality of one’s Torah activity
records.themeSummary: Concern about misuse can itself redirect learning toward its proper purpose.
records.originHebrew: וּבַגְּמָרָא (יוֹמָא ע״ב עַמּוּד ב׳) נִדְרַשׁ "לָמָּה זֶּה מְחִיר בְּיַד כְּסִיל" עַל שֶׁעוֹסְקִין בַּתּוֹרָה וְאֵין בָּהֶם יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם; וְרוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנַן הוּא לְהַרְגִּיז עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא כְּסִיל, וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה, פַּחַד יִצְחָק, אֵשׁ דִּקְדֻשָּׁה; וְהַפְּסֹלֶת מִמֶּנּוּ עֵשָׂו, כַּעַס, אֵשׁ שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע כֵּן הוּא לְגִרְסַת הַגְּאוֹנִים.
records.originEnglish: The Gemara expounds “Why is there a price in the hand of a fool?” concerning those who engage in Torah but have no awe of Heaven. The anger of the sages is to stir against the evil inclination so that one will not be a fool. This comes through awe, Isaac’s fear, holy fire; its waste is Esau—anger, the evil inclination’s fire. This is according to the Geonim’s reading.
records.targetHebrew: בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מוּתָּר אָדָם לִפְחוֹד, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרָכוֹת (ס.); הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּפְחַד שֶׁמָּא הוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם סַם הַמָּוֶת, וְעַל יְדֵי הַפַּחַד עַצְמוֹ מִתְמַתֵּק וְנַעֲשָׂה "מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ – לִשְׁמָהּ".
records.targetEnglish: In words of Torah a person is permitted to fear, as our sages say in Berakhot. That is, one should fear lest it be, God forbid, a poison of death; through the fear itself it is sweetened and becomes “from engagement not for its own sake, engagement for its own sake.”
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik distinguishes learned anger directed against the inclination from the foolishness of Torah study without awe. Tzidkat HaTzadik explains why fear concerning one’s Torah can be constructive: concern that the learning might become harmful can itself sweeten and redirect it. This clarifies the role of awe in the difference stated here.

records.themeTitle: The corrective force must stay within its needed measure
records.themeSummary: The captain’s counter-steering explains disciplined resistance without excess.
records.originHebrew: וְהַיְנוּ "רוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנַן דְּאִיהוּ טָב לְכָל סִטְרִין" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ, וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳): "לְעוֹלָם יַרְגִּיז אָדָם יֵצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע וְכוּלֵיהּ", וְהוּא הֵפֶךְ מִכַּעַס דִּכְתִיב: "כִּי כַעַס בְּחֵיק כְּסִילִים יָנוּחַ".
records.originEnglish: This is “the anger of the sages, which is good on every side,” as the Zohar says: “A person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination.” It is the opposite of the anger of which it is written, “Anger rests in the bosom of fools.”
records.targetHebrew: ועיקר הכעס, הציב השי"ת בזה העולם כענין דכתיב (משלי כ״ד:ו׳) כי בתחבולות תעשה לך מלחמה, וביאר בזה כבוד אזמו"ר זללה"ה כי הוא מלשון רב החובל, והיינו כמו רב החובל אשר אם רואה שהספינה נוטה לצד אחד נוטה הוא הספינה לצד השני, והגם שאם תנטה הספינה לצד שהוא נוטה ג"כ אינו טוב. מ"מ פועל זאת כדי להנצל שיעמוד הספינה על קו השוה. כך הוא כיון שיש עדיין בעולם תאות רעות, הציב השי"ת מדת הכעס, כי בזה יכול האדם להנצל מן תאוה. וכל זמן שאדם כועס כפי מה שצריך להצלה מתאוה זה נקרא רוגזא דרבנן, ומעט יותר אפילו כחוט השערה זה נקרא עבודה זרה ממש.
records.targetEnglish: God placed the power of anger in this world in the sense of “With strategies you shall wage war,” which my holy grandfather explained through the ship’s captain. If the captain sees the ship tilting to one side, he tilts it toward the other. Tilting toward that side would not itself be good either; he does it to escape danger and restore the ship to an even line. So, because harmful desires still exist in the world, God placed the quality of anger within it, through which a person can escape desire. As long as the anger is only to the extent needed to escape desire, it is called the anger of the sages. Even a hair’s breadth more is called actual idolatry.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik defines the holy agitation as stirring the good inclination against the bad, the opposite of anger resting with fools. Tiferet Yosef gives a precise image and limit: a captain steers against a dangerous tilt only to restore balance. The force needed to escape desire is distinguished sharply from even a small excess. This makes the origin’s distinction practical and exact.

records.themeTitle: The two awakenings call to one another
records.themeSummary: The plea for God to draw us and the call for us to return belong to one relationship.
records.originHebrew: שֶׁשְּׁנֵי הַגִּרְסָאוֹת אֲמִתִּיִּים: שֶׁמִּצַּד הָאָדָם הָעֵסֶק בְּחֹדֶשׁ זֶה: הָרוֹגֶז, "לְעוֹלָם יַרְגִּיז יֵצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע"; וּמִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קְדֻשַּׁת חֹדֶשׁ זֶה: "הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ בְּשֵׁינָה", עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה׳): "'אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה מִן הַמִּצְווֹת וְכוּלֵיהּ, וְלִבִּי עֵר' נִדְרַשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ עַל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁהוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל", וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְעוֹרֵר אֶת הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל אַף כִּי "אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה מִן הַמִּצְווֹת".
records.originEnglish: Both readings are true. From the person’s side, the work of this month is agitation: “Always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination.” From God’s side, the month’s holiness is “He made samekh rule over sleep”: “I sleep regarding the commandments, but my heart is awake,” which is expounded concerning the Holy One, Israel’s heart. God awakens the Jew even when “I sleep regarding the commandments.”
records.targetHebrew: כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּ״כְמַיִם הַפָּנִים״ וְגוֹ’, וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וְדִלְעֵילָּא מְעוֹרְרִים זֶה אֶת זֶה; רַק שֶׁאָנוּ אוֹמְרִים ״מָשְׁכֵנִי [אַחֲרֶיךָ נָּרוּצָה]״ וַ״הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ״, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא קוֹדֶמֶת לְעוֹרְרֵנוּ, וְאָנוּ נִמְשׁוֹךְ וְנָרוּץ אַחֲרָיו והשי“ת אוֹמֵר בְּהֵיפֶךְ ״שׁוּבוּ [אֵלַי וְאָשׁוּבָה אֲלֵיכֶם]״, וְעַל זֶה הוּא כָּל אֹרֶךְ הַגָּלוּת — שהשי”ת רוֹצֶה שֶׁנְּעוֹרֵר אֲנַחְנוּ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, וְאִם יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂים תְּשׁוּבָה מִיָּד נִגְאָלִים
records.targetEnglish: As is known from “As water reflects face to face,” awakening from below and awakening from above stir one another. We say, “Draw me; after You we shall run,” and “Return us,” asking that the awakening from above come first to awaken us, so that we will be drawn and run after Him. God, however, says the reverse: “Return to Me, and I will return to you.” The whole length of exile concerns this: God wishes us to awaken through an awakening from below, and if Israel repents they are immediately redeemed.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik reconciles the readings of anger and sleep through two sides: the person’s resistance and God’s awakening help. Takanat HaShavin describes the mutual movement explicitly through the different voices of “Return us” and “Return to Me.” This explains why the plea for an awakening from above can coexist with a demand for initiative below.

records.themeTitle: Effort can discover the gift that made it possible
records.themeSummary: Two descriptions of preparation meet when one recognizes the source of one’s strength.

records.originEnglish: Both readings are true. From the person’s side, the work of this month is agitation: “Always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination.” From God’s side, the month’s holiness is “He made samekh rule over sleep”: “I sleep regarding the commandments, but my heart is awake,” which is expounded concerning the Holy One, Israel’s heart. God awakens the Jew even when “I sleep regarding the commandments.”
records.targetHebrew: ובאמת אמר בזה כבוד אזמו"ר זללה"ה אשר אלו ואלו דברי אלהים חיים, היינו אם האדם מבקע את ההסתר מכיר אשר כח קדושתו אשר יש בו כח להרחיב את הד"ת, הוא הכל יען אשר יש בו קדושת שבת שקבוע וקיימא, ואז נותן לו השי"ת הד"ת בקביעות ויש לו חלק גם בקדושת שבת שקבוע וקיימא, אשר לזאת הקדושה אין אדם מגיע בפעולותיו, מ"מ יש לו חלק בה ג"כ:
records.targetEnglish: My holy grandfather explained that these and those are the words of the living God: when a person breaks through concealment, he recognizes that his power of holiness—the power to expand words of Torah—comes entirely from the holiness of Shabbat already permanently established within him. God then gives him words of Torah in an established way, and he has a share even in Shabbat’s permanent holiness. Although a person cannot reach that holiness through his actions, he nevertheless has a share in it as well.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik treats the human and divine descriptions of Kislev as both true. Tiferet Yosef similarly explains two descriptions of the preparation for Sinai: after breaking through concealment, a person recognizes that the power used in preparation was itself rooted in God’s established holiness. This clarifies how genuine human exertion and prior divine support can describe one process.

records.themeTitle: Yesterday’s victory still calls for today’s prayer
records.themeSummary: The inclination’s renewal makes the request for divine help essential.
records.originHebrew: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁלִיךְ עֶזְרוֹ רַק לַמְבַקְשִׁים עֶזְרוֹ בִּתְפִלָּה, כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "קָרוֹב הַשֵּׁם לְכָל קֹרְאָיו, לְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָאֻהוּ בֶאֱמֶת", וּכְעֵין מַה שֶּׁמְּבַקֶּשֶׁת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל: "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ הַשֵּׁם אֵלֶיךָ" וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וְנָשׁוּבָה" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוֹף אֵיכָה רַבָּה).
records.originEnglish: Nevertheless, God grants His help only to those who seek His help in prayer, as it is said, “The Lord is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth.” It resembles the community of Israel’s request, “Return us, Lord, to You,” and afterwards, “we shall return.”
records.targetHebrew: כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם בִּשְׁבִירַת הַיֵּצֶר בַּתַּאֲווֹת נִקְרָא חֵן וְיוֹפִי לְבַד, שֶׁהוּא שֶׁקֶר וָהֶבֶל שֶׁאֵינוֹ קִיּוּם לָעַד, כִּי הַיֵּצֶר מִתְגַּבֵּר בְּכָל יוֹם, וְאוּלַי מָחָר לֹא יְנַצְּחֶנּוּ. רַק הָעִיקָּר לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּעֶזְרוֹ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִבְטָח נֶאֱמָן, כִּי גוֹאֲלוֹ חָי.
records.targetEnglish: All a person’s effort in breaking the inclination in matters of desire is called only grace and beauty, which are false and vain: they do not endure forever, for the inclination grows stronger every day, and perhaps tomorrow one will not overcome it. The essential thing is to ask God to help him. This is a reliable trust, for his Redeemer lives.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik requires the person who awaits an awakening from above to ask for help in prayer. Tzidkat HaTzadik explains why the request cannot be replaced by confidence in past self-restraint: the inclination renews its attack, and yesterday’s victory does not secure tomorrow. This gives a concrete reason for the continuing prayer demanded here.
records.translationProvenance: New English translations of the unchanged canonical Hebrew excerpts, prepared for this editorial connection. The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: Prayer places the receiving vessel within reach
records.themeSummary: The gift may be beyond one’s measure, while the humble request is one’s available work.
records.originHebrew: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁלִיךְ עֶזְרוֹ רַק לַמְבַקְשִׁים עֶזְרוֹ בִּתְפִלָּה, כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "קָרוֹב הַשֵּׁם לְכָל קֹרְאָיו, לְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָאֻהוּ בֶאֱמֶת", וּכְעֵין מַה שֶּׁמְּבַקֶּשֶׁת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל: "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ הַשֵּׁם אֵלֶיךָ" וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וְנָשׁוּבָה" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוֹף אֵיכָה רַבָּה).
records.originEnglish: Nevertheless, God grants His help only to those who seek His help in prayer, as it is said, “The Lord is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth.” It resembles the community of Israel’s request, “Return us, Lord, to You,” and afterwards, “we shall return.”
records.targetHebrew: כי כן הציב השי"ת בעוה"ז שהכלי הוא של האדם וזה נקרא יראת שמים, ומה הוא הכלי של האדם, העיקר הוא דמאיך גרמהי למשרא עליה גאותא דקוב"ה, וכדכתיב, ויהי האדם לנפש חיה ומתרגם לרוח ממללא. ואיתא בזוה"ק (תזריע מו:) ודא היא דסלקא לעילא וממללא קמי מלכא קדישא ועיילא בכל תרעין ולית דימחי בידהא ועל דא אתקרי רוחא ממללא וכו'. והיינו שהאדם עומד בתפלה לפני השי"ת אז משפיע לו השי"ת הד"ת. ובאמת הד"ת שמשפיע השי"ת הם כמה עלאין וכמה יקירין, כמו דאיתא בזוה"ק (שם), אך הכלי שמציב האדם זה הוא בידו של אדם. וזה, כי קרוב אליך הדבר מאד בפיך ובלבבך לעשותו, היינו כשהאדם מאיך גרמיה למישרא עליה גאותא דקוב"ה וזה הוא הכלי של אדם, אז משפיע לו השי"ת הד"ת מכמה עלאין:
records.targetEnglish: God established in this world that the vessel belongs to the person, and this is called awe of Heaven. What is the person’s vessel? Principally, to lower oneself so that the majesty of the Holy One may rest upon one. “The human being became a living soul” is translated “a speaking spirit.” The Zohar says that this spirit ascends and speaks before the holy King, enters all the gates, and none can stop it; it is therefore called a speaking spirit. When the person stands before God in prayer, God bestows words of Torah upon him. Those words of Torah are indeed very exalted and precious; but the vessel the person establishes is in his own hands. This is “The matter is very near to you, in your mouth and your heart, to do it”: when one lowers oneself so that the Holy One’s majesty may rest upon one, this is the person’s vessel, and God bestows the exalted words of Torah.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik’s call to seek help in prayer can be understood through Tiferet Yosef’s distinction between the exalted gift and the receiving vessel. Words of Torah may be very high, but humbling oneself and standing in prayer is the humanly accessible vessel. This explains the small initiative that can accompany awaiting help from above.

The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: Use the given powers while trusting for help beyond them
records.themeSummary: Reliance on Torah, wisdom, and service accompanies confidence in a greater deliverance.
records.originHebrew: גַּם צָרִיךְ עַל כָּל פָּנִים אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בִּתְפִלָּה, לְבַקֵּשׁ עֶזְרָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מִן הַיֵּצֶר הַמְבַקֵּשׁ לַהֲמִיתוֹ וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ, וְאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹזֵר לוֹ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא. וְזֶה מוֹרֶה אוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ: "סוֹמֵךְ הַשֵּׁם לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ; וְכֵן מוֹרֶה אוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ עַל סֻכַּת דָּוִד הַנּוֹפֶלֶת, שֶׁמַּקִּיף כְּסֻכָּה לְהָגֵן עַל מְבַקְשֵׁי עֶזְרָתוֹ לִהְיוֹת סוֹמֵךְ לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים. וּמִצַּד הָאָדָם הָעֵסֶק בְּחֹדֶשׁ זֶה: לְהַרְגִּיז הַיֵּצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּכָל כֹּחוֹ, עַד שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ מִצִּדּוֹ.
records.originEnglish: At least an awakening from below in prayer is also needed: to ask His help against the inclination that seeks to kill him, which he cannot overcome. God then helps through an awakening from above. Samekh indicates “The Lord supports all who fall,” and the fallen sukkah of David: it surrounds like a sukkah, protecting those who seek His help. From the person’s side, the work of this month is to stir the good inclination against the bad with all his strength, until he cannot overcome it from his own side.
records.targetHebrew: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם זֶהוּ רַק בִּטָּחוֹן, אֲבָל "יִשָּׁעֵן" – מִשְׁעָן הוּא יוֹתֵר, וּמַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּיָדוֹ וְנִשְׁעָן עָלָיו, זֶהוּ "בֵּאלֹהָיו", כִּידוּעַ דְּשֵׁם זֶה מוֹרֶה עַל כֹּחוֹת הַמּוּטְבָּעִים בַּבְּרוּאִים, וֶ"אֱלֹהָיו" רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כֹּחוֹתָיו שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שֶׁנָּתַן לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְכַלְכֵּל עַצְמוֹ עַל יָדוֹ בְּכָל צְרָכָיו בְּעֵצוֹת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְחָכְמָה וַעֲבוֹדָה – בָּזֶה הוּא עִיקַּר הַשְּׁעִינָה. וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יִבְטַח בִּישׁוּעָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִכֹּחוֹ גַּם כֵּן, כִּי אֵין מַעְצוֹר לַה', וְהֵן לֹא קָצְרָה יָדוֹ מֵהוֹשִׁיעַ:
records.targetEnglish: Nevertheless, this is trust. “He shall lean” means more: the support that is in his hands, on which he leans, is “on his God.” As is known, this name signifies the powers implanted in created beings. “His God” means the powers he has, which God gave him to sustain himself in all his needs through counsel from Torah, wisdom, and service. This is his principal reliance. Yet he should also trust in deliverance beyond his power, for nothing restrains the Lord, and His hand is not too short to save.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik retains prayer and effort with all one’s strength before the point of inability. Tzidkat HaTzadik distinguishes the powers one can actually lean on—God-given Torah, wisdom, and service—from trust in a deliverance beyond those powers. This explains why awaiting divine support does not cancel the work already placed in one’s hands.

The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: The limits observed in service form a vessel for greater help
records.themeSummary: Torah and mitzvot prepare a finite person to receive what exceeds his own power.
records.originHebrew: אַךְ הוּא דַּוְקָא כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם בְּשֵׁינָה סוּר מֵרָע, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה י״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): "שֶׁמָּא יֹאמַר: אֵלֵךְ וְאֶתְגָּרֶה בְּשֵׁינָה וְכוּלֵיהּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: 'וַעֲשֵׂה טוֹב'". גַּם צָרִיךְ עַל כָּל פָּנִים אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בִּתְפִלָּה, לְבַקֵּשׁ עֶזְרָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מִן הַיֵּצֶר הַמְבַקֵּשׁ לַהֲמִיתוֹ וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ, וְאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹזֵר לוֹ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא.
records.originEnglish: This applies specifically when the person is asleep while avoiding evil. As the Gemara says, might one say, “I will go and provoke sleep”? Scripture says, “And do good.” At least an awakening from below in prayer is also needed: to ask His help against the inclination that seeks to kill him, which he cannot overcome. God then helps him through an awakening from above.
records.targetHebrew: וגם אפילו שהולך האדם דרך כל הסייגים והגדרים מתורה ומצות, עם כל זה נמי מצינו בש"ס (סוכה נב:) אלמלא הקב"ה עוזרו וכו'. ולהנחיל את האדם שפע חסדו ית' טרם שהולך בעבודתו דרך כל הסייגים מתורה ומצות זאת אי אפשר כלל כי האדם מצידו הוא בעל גבול ושפע חסדו ית' הוא באמת בלי גבול, ואיך יתכן לבעל גבול לקבל בלי גבול. אולם אחר שהולך אדם בעבודתו דרך כל הסייגים מתורה ומצוות, אז נעשה כלי לקבל גם מה שהוא בלי גבול, שיהיה מכיר היטב החיבור מהשמים לארץ. וזה החיבור נקרא גבורות גשמים, ועל זה איתא כאן בגמ' ומנלן דבתפלה דתניא לאהבה את ד' אלהיכם וגו' איזה היא עבודה שבלב הוי אומר זו תפלה, וכתיב בתריה ונתתי מטר ארצכם בעתו יורה ומלקוש, היינו שאחר עבודת האדם נותן לו השי"ת כח התפלה, וחותם עליו אשר בעומק לבו נמצא אצלו כ"כ חוזק אמונה ובטחון בלי גבול, עד שמגיע לו בשורת הדין ע"י יגיע כפיו השפעתו ית' שהוא בלי גבול:
records.targetEnglish: Even when a person proceeds in service through all the fences and boundaries of Torah and commandments, we still find in the Talmud, “Were the Holy One not to help him…” Yet bestowing the flow of His kindness upon a person before he proceeds in service through all those boundaries is impossible: a person is finite, while the flow of His kindness is truly without limit. How could the finite receive the infinite? Once a person proceeds in service through the fences of Torah and commandments, he becomes a vessel to receive even what has no limit, recognizing well the connection between Heaven and earth. This connection is called the powers of rain. The Gemara therefore asks, how do we know this is in prayer? “‘To love the Lord your God…’—what is service of the heart? Prayer”; afterwards it is written, “I will give your land’s rain in its season.” After the person’s work, God gives him the power of prayer and attests that such firm, unbounded faith and trust exist in his heart’s depths that, through the work of his own hands, he is fittingly entitled to the divine flow that has no limit.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik explicitly requires avoiding evil, praying, and exerting oneself with all one’s strength. Tiferet Yosef explains why preparation matters even though a person still cannot prevail without God’s help: working through Torah’s boundaries makes a finite person into a vessel for an unbounded gift. The quoted passage retains both the need for preparation and the continuing need for divine assistance.

The complete originating section and the complete target paragraph were read in context. This comparison does not claim that one author explicitly cites the other.

records.themeTitle: One shared whole can reveal different particular strengths
records.themeSummary: Differences of soul and time do not erase the unity that contains them.
records.originHebrew: וְ"אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים": שֶׁיֵּשׁ נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַכִּיר בָּהֶם שֶׁצְּרִיכִין הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מִצִּדָּם לְהַרְגִּיז עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע; וְיֵשׁ נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ סוֹמֵךְ לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים, כְּמַאֲמַר: "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ הַשֵּׁם אֵלֶיךָ" וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וְנָשׁוּבָה". וְכֵן פֵּרוּשׁ "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים", שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד אָמַר כְּפִי שֹׁרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתוֹ; וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַכִּיר שֹׁרֶשׁ נִשְׁמַת כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְכֵן הַהַנְהָגָה עִמּוֹ. אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, אַף מִי שֶׁהוּא מִכְּלַל הַצְּרִיכִין עֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא עַל כָּל פָּנִים לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לַהשֵּׁם וּלְבַקֵּשׁ עֶזְרוֹ;
records.originEnglish: “These and those are the words of the living God”: there are souls whom God knows to need effort from their own side, stirring against the evil inclination; and there are souls for whom God “supports all who fall,” in the sense of “Return us, Lord, to You,” and afterwards, “we shall return.” Each spoke according to the root of his soul, and God knows the root of every Jewish soul and how to guide it. Nevertheless, even one who belongs among those needing God’s help must at least awaken from below by praying to God and asking His help.
records.targetHebrew: כִּידוּעַ דִּי״ב חֹדֶשׁ הֵם נֶגֶד י״ב שְׁבָטִים שֶׁלְּכָל שֵׁבֶט יֵשׁ מַעֲלָה וְכֹחַ מְיוּחָד שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא מִתְיַיחֵד וְנִרְשָׁם מִשְּׁאָר הַשְּׁבָטִים, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה נֶחְשָׁב לְשֵׁבֶט בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּלָּם ״גּוֹי אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ״ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב ז:כג), שֶׁכּוּלָּם אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ וְכָל אֶחָד מֵהֶם כָּלוּל מִכָּל הַמַּעֲלוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא מִתְגַּלֶּה בִּפְרָט בַּנֶּפֶשׁ הַמְיוּחָד לָזֶה וְיָדוּעַ דְּכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ ״עוֹלָם וְשָׁנָה וְנֶפֶשׁ״ (סֵפֶר יְצִירָה) וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ נְפָשׁוֹת חֲלוּקוֹת, כָּךְ יֵשׁ זְמַנִּים חֲלוּקִים וּמְקוֹמוֹת חֲלוּקִים וּכְלַל חֲלוּקַת הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל לְי״ב שְׁבָטִים, הוּא חֲלוּקַת הַמְּקוֹמוֹת דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל לְי״ב גְּבוּלֵי אֲלַכְסוֹן שֶׁל הָעוֹלָם הַנִּזְכָּר בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה, וְהַשָּׁנָה לְי״ב חֹדֶשׁ וְסִדְרָן שֶׁל חֳדָשִׁים לַשְּׁבָטִים יֵשׁ בָּהֶם כַּמָּה פָּנִים, וְעִנְיָנִים גְּדוֹלִים וַעֲמוּקִים יֵשׁ בָּזֶה אֵיךְ כָּל הַסְּדָרִים אֱמֶת,
records.targetEnglish: The twelve months correspond to the twelve tribes. Each tribe has a particular excellence and power through which it is distinguished from the other tribes and reckoned as a tribe in its own right. Although all Israel are “one nation on earth,” truly one, and each contains all the excellences found in the whole of Israel, a particular excellence becomes manifest in the soul specially corresponding to it. Every matter has world, year, and soul: as souls differ, so do times and places. The general division of Israel’s souls into twelve tribes corresponds to the world’s twelve diagonal boundaries and the year’s twelve months. There are several arrangements of the months and tribes, with great and deep matters involved in how all the arrangements are true.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik explains opposing spiritual approaches through each soul’s root and God’s knowledge of how to guide it. Machshavot Charutz supplies the underlying pattern: although each member of Israel contains the whole, a particular strength becomes especially manifest in its corresponding soul, time, and place. This helps explain differentiated routes without turning one person’s route into a universal prescription.

records.themeTitle: Different souls require different forms of discipline
records.themeSummary: Levi’s caution and Simeon’s different path illustrate why one route cannot simply be copied.

records.targetHebrew: וְכֵן גַּם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְצְאוּ נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁמֻּתָּרִים לְהַכְנִיס עַצְמָם יוֹתֵר בִּסְפֵיקוֹת מִנְּפָשׁוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת אַף שֶׁאֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב, כְּמוֹ הָעִנְיָן שֶׁל שִׁמְעוֹן וְדִינָה, כִּי לֵוִי לֹא חָפַץ לְקַחְתָּהּ כִּי יָרֵא לְנַפְשׁוֹ פֶּן אֵין כַּוָּנָתוֹ בְּעֹמֶק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, כִּי כָל שֵׁבֶט לֵוִי הֵם בְּיִרְאָה וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּת מִסָּפֵק אֶצְלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אֶצְלָם (מַלְאָכִי בֵּית, הֵא) "וָאֶתְּנֵם לוֹ מוֹרָא" וְכוּלֵי וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יָצְאוּ מֵאִתָּם כֹּהֲנִים שֶׁנִּכְנָסִים לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים, וְעַל כֵּן נִתְבָּרֵר הַחַיִּים שֶׁלָּהֶם מִיָּד כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר בְּפָרָשַׁת קֹרַח בְּהַמַּטּוֹת [דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל וַיֹּאמֶר הַשֵּׁם]. אֲבָל שִׁמְעוֹן הִכְנִיס עַצְמוֹ בְּסָפֵק וְאָמַר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁאֲנִי מַחְזִיק עַצְמִי לְנוֹאֵף, וְנָשָׂא אֶת דִּינָה וְהִכְנִיס אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּדָבָר הַצָּרִיךְ בָּרֵר, כִּי אָמַר שֶׁהוּא בָּטוּחַ בַּהַשֵּׁם שֶׁיְּבָרְרוֹ לְטוֹב שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ לֹא הָיְתָה רַק לְהוֹצִיאָהּ מִשְּׁכֶם וְכָל כַּוָּנָתוֹ הָיְתָה רַק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה צָרִיךְ כָּל שֵׁבֶט שִׁמְעוֹן לְבֵרוּרִין בִּדְבָרִים כָּאֵלֶּה, כְּגוֹן זִמְרִי שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר גַּם כֵּן שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ טוֹב כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר בִּמְקוֹמוֹ [פָּרָשַׁת בָּלָק דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל וְהִנֵּה] וְלֶעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר שֵׁבֶט שִׁמְעוֹן יִהְיֶה מַעֲלָתוֹ גָּדוֹל מִשֶּׁל לֵוִי.
records.targetEnglish: Even within Israel there are souls permitted to enter matters of uncertainty more than other souls, although both descend from Jacob, as in the matter of Simeon and Dinah. Levi did not wish to take her, fearing lest his intention not be for the sake of Heaven in its depth; the tribe of Levi is marked by awe and withdrawal from uncertainty, as it is written, “I gave them awe.” Priests who enter the innermost sanctuary therefore came from them, and their life was clarified immediately, as will be explained concerning the staffs in Korach. Simeon, however, entered the uncertainty, saying, “God forbid that I should regard myself as sexually immoral.” He married Dinah and entered a matter requiring clarification, trusting that God would clarify it for good, since his intention was only to bring her out of Shechem and was wholly for the sake of Heaven. The whole tribe of Simeon therefore required clarification in such matters, as with Zimri, who likewise said his intention was good, as will be explained in its place. In the future, when the tribe of Simeon is clarified, its degree will be greater than Levi’s.
records.explanation: Pri Tzadik relates the difference between exertion and reliance on help to individual soul roots, while requiring prayer of everyone. Mei HaShiloach gives a concrete example of different disciplines within Israel: Levi withdraws from uncertainty, while Simeon enters a matter that requires further clarification. The quoted target retains the later need for clarification, including Zimri, and does not make Simeon’s confidence a general permission. Pri Tzadik’s universal requirement of prayer remains his own explicit qualification.
